item.title: Wolf: easier culls, consultation closes today
item.description: The Federal Council proposes making wolf culls easier.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Council proposes making wolf culls easier. - Environmentalists are calling for the project to be suspended. - USC supports the revision, but considers it insufficient. - The new law has been in force since February 1, 2025.
## Key facts - Proponent → Federal Council, at Parliament’s request - Subject → Revision of the Hunting Act (LCP) - Consultation → Expected to close today - Entry into force → February 1, 2025 - Period mentioned → February and March - Objective → Curb the growth of the wolf population
## The revision of the Hunting Act At Parliament’s request, the Federal Council has proposed a revision of the Hunting Act (LCP) that provides for new provisions facilitating the culling of wolves. The proposal divides environmental and agricultural organizations.
During the consultation procedure, which closes today, Pro Natura, BirdLife Svizzera and Gruppo Lupo Svizzera (GLS) submitted a joint position statement. The three NGOs are calling for the project to be put on hold so that it can be examined as part of the broad revision of the LCP already announced by the government.
They point out that the new federal regulations on hunting and the protection of wild mammals and birds entered into force on February 1, 2025. According to the organizations, experience with this legal framework must be gained before the legislation is amended again.
### The positions of the parties The environmental NGOs, which consider the wolf a protected species, reject the proposal to expand the legal authority to cull it. They object in particular to the possibility of killing canids even in areas where a hunting ban is in force.
The Swiss Farmers’ Union (USC), on the other hand, particularly welcomes the possibility of culling problem wolves throughout the year. However, it considers the planned changes insufficient: the expanded intervention options would continue to face significant obstacles. In the USC’s view, the requirement for at least two attacks on livestock kept under protected conditions in an area subject to a hunting ban is excessive.
The Swiss Alpine Economy Society (SSEA) also supports the revision. In its view, the experience of the last three years has revealed gaps with serious consequences for mountain agriculture. The association hopes for rapid implementation and the possibility of removing isolated wolves or packs when the population reaches a predetermined number of specimens.
The project would authorize the culling of problem wolves—namely, specimens that attack flocks and herds or pose a danger to humans—throughout the year, including February and March. The objective is to curb population growth, while the number of packs has continued to increase despite regulatory measures in operation since 2023. According to the Federal Council, the provisions facilitating culling remain compatible with international conventions: the species’ status has changed from “strictly protected” to “protected.” ## Three points of contention The project's practical scope focuses on timing, territory, and the conditions for intervention. The proposal concerns not only the possibility of culling a problem wolf, but also the time of year and the areas in which action would be permitted.
The first element is timing. Culling would be authorized throughout the year, including the breeding period indicated as February and March. For USC, this extension is an improvement, because problem wolves could be culled without a seasonal pause. Environmental organizations, on the other hand, regard it as a further legal possibility for killing a protected species.
The second element is territory. NGOs object in particular to the possibility of intervening in areas where a hunting ban is in force. USC starts from a different concern: it considers the threshold of at least two attacks on livestock under protected conditions, occurring in an area subject to a hunting ban, excessive. The disagreement therefore concerns both the scope of the authority to cull and the level of conditions required.
### Comparison of the conditions | Issue | Provision or request described in the source | Position recorded | |---|---|---| | Period | Culling of problem wolves all year round, including in February and March | USC is in favor; NGOs oppose new legal possibilities | | Zones | Possibility of killing wolves even in hunting-ban areas | Environmental NGOs particularly challenge it | | Attacks | At least two attacks in protected situations within a hunting-ban area | USC considers the requirement excessive | | Population | Removal of individual wolves or packs after a predetermined number has been reached | SSEA views this possibility positively |
The third element is the population-related criterion. SSEA formulates its request in relation to the number of specimens, while USC refers to attacks on livestock. These are two different ways of describing when intervention should become possible, both of which are present in the discussion on the revision.
For mountain agriculture, SSEA links gaps in the legislation to serious consequences and calls for rapid implementation. For environmental organizations, the fact that the new law entered into force on February 1, 2025, makes it preferable to gain experience before intervening in the legislation again. The Federal Council, on the other hand, presents the revision as a tool to curb the growth of the wolf population, which has increased despite the regulatory measures in force since 2023.
The project is also presented as respecting international conventions, because the wolf's status has changed from “strictly protected” to “protected”. The Swiss discussion therefore revolves around the balance between species protection and the safeguarding of mountain agriculture, without the source yet announcing a definitive outcome of the procedure. ## Following the dossier without confusing the stages The procedure indicated by the source ends today. To read the revision correctly, it is useful to distinguish the law that has already entered into force from the proposal submitted for consultation and check, point by point, which conditions are actually described.
### Five reading steps 1. Separate the legislation and the proposal. Since February 1, 2025, the new federal legislation governing the hunting and protection of wild mammals and birds has been in force. The amendment now under discussion is instead a proposal by the Federal Council, drawn up under a mandate from Parliament.
2. Identify the problematic wolf. The definition contained in the draft concerns individuals that attack flocks and herds or pose a danger to humans. The text therefore does not present culling as applying indiscriminately to every wolf.
3. Check the calendar. The easing applies year-round and also includes the breeding period in February and March. This is what must be distinguished from the regulatory measures already in force since 2023.
4. Verify the location and threshold for attacks. The proposal also takes hunting-ban zones into account. However, USC considers excessive the condition requiring at least two attacks on livestock under protected conditions to have occurred in one of these zones.
5. Compare the population criterion. SSEA is in favor of culling individual wolves or packs as soon as the population reaches the predetermined number of specimens. This request should be kept distinct from the attack criterion mentioned by USC.
This route makes it possible to read the three operational issues separately: the time of year, the areas in which culling would be possible, and the conditions necessary to intervene. It also helps avoid confusing the positions: the NGOs are calling for the project to be suspended and included in the major revision of the LCP; USC supports it but considers it insufficient; SSEA hopes for its rapid implementation.
For those following mountain agriculture, the central reference is the serious consequences reported by SSEA over the last three years. For those concerned with wolf protection, the central point remains the status of the species, defined as protected, and opposition to further culling options. Finally, the proposal must be distinguished from the outcome of the consultation: the source describes the draft and the positions taken, not a final decision.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/lupo%3a-abbattimenti-facilitati%3b-no-da-ambientalisti%2c-s%c3%ac-da-contadini/92225907)*

item.title: Three million digital letters in six months
item.description: La Posta presented the first interim report on the digital letter, recording seven million digital mailings in six months, three million of which were letters.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Seven million digital mailings in six months - Three million were letters - 960'000 accounts for receiving letters in the Posta app - An app update is planned for November
## Key facts - Report date → 15 October 2026 - Period under review → six months since introduction - Digital mailings → 7 million - Digital letters → 3 million - Accounts opened → 960'000 - Consultations on the app → 3'000 per month - New feature → legally valid electronic signature
On 15 October 2026, La Posta presented the first interim report six months after the introduction of the digital letter. According to reports, this is the first experience of this kind in its 177-year history. The overall figure is seven million digital mailings, three million of which were letters.
### The service's first report
Nicole Burth, head of La Posta's Digital Service unit, explained to Radiogiornale that 960'000 customers had decided to receive digital letters in La Posta's app. The number is growing, but the figure should be read as the number of accounts opened. It therefore does not mean that all customers have already actually used the service.
La Posta considers the report positive, while indicating some developments that should proceed more quickly. The point concerns above all the amount of mail available through the platform. For private users, Burth explained, the service becomes interesting when a lot of correspondence passes through it. Large companies are also needed to achieve this result.
The first major users have already switched to digital letters, while considerable potential remains among banks and insurers. The report thus compares recipient adoption with platform use by major senders.
Among the announced new features is the legally valid electronic signature. The example cited is that of a real-estate agency sending a rental contract: the future tenant will be able to sign it electronically. It will also be possible to modify and resend forms online, for example.
The app will be updated in November. The improvements were also developed based on customer feedback, with customers currently submitting 3'000 requests for advice about the app each month. On the subject of security, Burth described digital protection as an ongoing process: La Posta must keep updating and improving, but theft cannot be completely ruled out, just as a letter can be stolen in the real world. For anyone considering the digital letter, the practical point is not simply having an account. The service becomes more attractive when a significant amount of mail passes through the same platform: this is the condition identified by the head of Digital Service. Individual users therefore face a value proposition that depends on senders' behavior, not just on their own enrollment.
### Value depends on senders
The arrival of the first major users confirms that organizations have already begun using it, while Posta points to considerable potential still remaining. Banks and insurance companies are specifically cited as sectors in which the digital letter could gain further ground. For the recipient, the practical consequence is that the account is the point of access, while its practical usefulness increases when more communications are actually sent through the application.
Electronic signatures introduce a second level of use. It is not merely a matter of receiving a document: in the example given of a lease sent by a real estate agency, the future tenant will be able to sign it with legal validity. The same platform will also allow users to edit and resend forms online. The operational promise described by Posta is therefore to simplify and streamline document-related processes.
This feature should not, however, be confused with an absolute guarantee against digital risk. Questions about security were asked in connection with cyberattacks and data theft. Nicole Burth's answer presents security as a continuous process requiring constant updates and improvements. Posta considers itself at the forefront on this issue, but acknowledges that theft cannot be ruled out completely. The comparison with a physical letter is explicit: even in the real world, a letter can be stolen.
To understand the service correctly, it is therefore useful to distinguish three aspects: access to the application, the presence of senders and usable documents, and the level of security, which remains the subject of ongoing work. Posta does not present digitization as perfect protection, but as an evolving channel, with features intended to make certain operations more straightforward. To use the service based on the functions described, the operational sequence can remain concise and faithful to what La Posta has announced.
### From the account to document functions
1. Choose digital receipt in the La Posta application. The account figure concerns customers who have decided to receive letters digitally in the app: this is the step described for joining the service.
2. Distinguish opening an account from actual use. La Posta specifies that the count of opened accounts does not mean that all of them have already used the service. The check to carry out is therefore tied to actual use of the function, not just registration.
3. Consider the update announced for November. La Posta linked the app's evolution to improvements that also arose from customer feedback. The time reference provided for this update is November.
4. Use the electronic signature when the new function becomes available. The publicized scenario concerns a rental contract sent by a real estate agency: the future tenant will be able to affix a legally valid electronic signature.
5. Manage forms online. The announced function will allow documents to be edited and sent back online, rather than merely received.
### The final check
Before considering an operation complete, the practical criterion is to verify which of the announced functions applies to the document: receipt, signing, editing or resending. La Posta's announcement describes these possibilities as developments of the service intended to make it easier to use.
On the security front, the practical rule is to keep expectations realistic. La Posta defines digital security as an ongoing process and acknowledges that theft cannot be completely ruled out. This serves as a warning about using the channel, without erasing the fact that even a letter in the real world can be stolen.
For support, the reference provided is the flow of customer requests: there are currently 3'000 requests for advice about the app per month. The figure shows that support is part of the service experience, while the November update will be the next step indicated by La Posta.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4166593)*

item.title: Taxes in Zurich: the three levels and how it works
item.description: The Swiss tax system is structured at three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Swiss tax system has three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal - Each Canton has its own law and multiplier - The Municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax - AFC/ESTV administers direct federal tax and VAT; the Canton administers the rest
## Key facts - Levels → federal direct tax (IFD), cantonal tax, municipal tax - Federal authority → AFC/ESTV for IFD and VAT - Cantonal authority → cantonal and municipal taxes - Municipal rule → multiplier applied to cantonal tax - Indexed figures → updated every year
Three levels make up the Swiss tax system: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. For the Canton of Zurich, rates, brackets and deductions must therefore be read within this framework, distinguishing what belongs to the Confederation from what depends on the Canton and the municipality.
Each Canton has its own law and its own multiplier. The municipal component uses the municipality's multiplier on the cantonal tax. Therefore, the municipal figure must be read together with the cantonal rule, without replacing it with a federal parameter.
The federal level is handled by AFC/ESTV, which is responsible for direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations, on the other hand, oversee cantonal and municipal taxes. This distinction also indicates the first point of reference: for the rules of the Canton of Zurich and for the municipal component, consult the cantonal tax administration, while AFC/ESTV remains the reference for IFD and VAT.
### Responsibilities not to be confused
The tax framework exists alongside social security and health insurance, but does not coincide with them. UFAS/BSV is responsible for social security, including AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, and does not set taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not determine tax rates.
LAMal/KVG is mandatory health insurance for residents, with per-capita premiums and a premium reduction managed at cantonal level. It is neither a tax nor a wage contribution. The distinction serves to prevent including in the tax calculation items that belong to social security or healthcare.
For the rates, brackets and permitted deductions in the Canton of Zurich, the operational reference remains the official documentation of the cantonal tax administration. The same channel indicates the submission deadline to meet and the online portal to use. Figures subject to indexation must instead be verified for the reference year, because some amounts change every year. ## Rates, brackets and deductions: how to avoid incorrect comparisons
The most concrete way to assess the tax burden in Zurich is to separate the three components before comparing rates or deductions. A value referring to direct federal tax does not automatically describe the cantonal share, while the municipal multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax.
| Component | Reference | What to verify | |---|---|---| | Direct federal tax | AFC/ESTV | federal level | | Cantonal tax | cantonal administration | the Canton’s law, rates and brackets | | Municipal tax | Municipality’s multiplier | application to the cantonal tax |
In the Canton of Zurich, this distinction changes how one searches for a deduction. The item to be applied must be verified in the relevant cantonal rules and not derived from a list referring to another Canton. The same care is needed for brackets: each Canton has its own law and the municipal result depends on the multiplier established for the Municipality.
Hypothetical scenario: a person takes a rate or deduction found for another Canton and transfers it into the Zurich tax return. The problem is not merely the number selected, but the tax level to which that number belongs. Before using it, it must be related back to the cantonal rule, the municipal component and, where necessary, direct federal tax.
Comparing disposable income and the cost of living then requires a second filter. AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG belong to social security and must not be confused with taxes. LAMal/KVG also follows a different logic: it is compulsory for residents, has per-capita premiums and provides for premiums that vary by Canton or region, in addition to a cantonal premium reduction. It is not a tax and is not a payroll contribution.
This separates the tax calculation from the family’s overall budget. A tax deduction, a social security contribution and a health insurance premium are not the same item, even when they all affect available funds. For accurate comparisons, the three components must therefore be read according to the authority and rule governing them. ## How to proceed with the tax return in the Canton of Zurich
The practical procedure begins with correctly identifying the jurisdictions involved. Generic figures valid throughout Switzerland are not needed: what is needed is the cantonal law, the municipal multiplier and the official information for the year in question.
### Five operational steps
1. Separate the three tax components: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. This distinction prevents using a federal figure for a cantonal or municipal component.
2. Identify the correct authority. For IFD and VAT, the reference is AFC/ESTV; for cantonal and municipal taxes, consult the cantonal tax administration.
3. Check the official source of the Canton of Zurich for the rates, brackets, permitted deductions and filing deadline. The date should not be reconstructed using a generic calendar or a rule from another Canton.
4. Use the online portal of the cantonal tax administration to follow the tax return procedure. The portal is the operational point of reference for the information and steps required by the cantonal authority.
5. Before submitting, check the reference year of the figures used. The figures indexed annually include the pillar 3a maximum, the LPP/BVG coordination threshold or deduction, the AD/AC maximum, the LAMal/KVG average premiums and the median salary.
### Figures and deadlines to check
In tax planning, it is not advisable to automatically carry over amounts already used in a previous year. For indexed figures, the practical rule is always to verify the value applicable in the year in question with the official source. The same check applies to the filing deadline and the instructions on the cantonal portal.
If the calculation starts from the payslip, AVS/AHV, LPP/BVG and LAMal/KVG must be kept separate from taxes. This labeling makes the transition from income to available budget easier to read without turning premiums or contributions into tax rates.
For an initial check of the relationship between income and taxes, use the calcolatore stipendio/imposte and consult the guide to the dichiarazione delle imposte.

item.title: Cyberattack: Zurich pension fund and Swiss Post hit
item.description: The attack on the supplier dates back to the end of September.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The attack on the supplier dates back to late September. - PKZH is investigating the stolen personal data of insured persons. - Funds and pension payments were not affected. - For Posta, it is unclear whether the data has been compromised.
## Key facts - Vendor → external software company - Connection → PKZH data transmitted for a new management system - PKZH → criminal complaint filed - Posta → attack confirmed, insured persons' data still uncertain - Benefits → pension funds and pension benefits not at risk
### The vendor at the center of the attack A cyberattack targeting an external software vendor affected the City of Zurich's pension fund and, with the situation still unclear, Posta's pension fund. The attack dates back to late September. PKZH explained that its data had been transmitted to the vendor in preparation for the transition to a new management system.
For insured persons, the key issue is the distinction between personal data and the management of pension assets. According to PKZH, neither pension assets nor pension payments appear to have been involved. The administrative system used to manage the assets and pay pensions would likewise not have been affected by the attack. PKZH filed a criminal complaint and is reconstructing the extent of the data theft, both in terms of the information affected and the number of people involved.
In the worst-case scenario, the data leak from the Zurich pension fund would concern personal contact information, including name, address, email and telephone number. The scenario envisaged could also include the AVS insurance number, marital status and partner information, IBAN details and other pension-related information, such as insured income and assets. This description concerns the worst-case scenario, while the assessment of the actual extent of the leak is still ongoing.
Posta's pension fund also announced that it had fallen victim to the attack on the vendor. However, it is not yet clear whether insured persons' data were compromised. Potentially affected information includes pension data, contact details and email address, as well as name, address, date of birth and AVS number. Posta specifies that pension assets and pension benefits are not at risk.
The case also involves other pension funds. Last week, it emerged that data had been stolen from the Bernese pension fund and the Bernese teachers' insurance fund. The picture therefore remains mixed for now: for PKZH, investigations into the scope are ongoing; for Posta, it has not been clarified whether insured persons' data were compromised, while the communications cited confirm that the attack on the vendor affected multiple pension institutions. ## What it means for insured persons For an insured person, the main practical point is the distinction between the possible theft of information and the security of assets. The statements do not describe the same situation for every fund: PKZH is determining the scope of the data, while Posta has not yet established whether the insured persons' data has been compromised. In both cases, however, the communication distinguishes personal data from pension benefits.
### Two distinct levels | Fund or institution | What the statement indicates | Open question | |---|---|---| | PKZH | Data transmitted to the supplier; funds, payments and administrative system not affected | Information stolen and number of people | | Posta pension fund | Attacked; assets and benefits not at risk | Whether the insured persons' data was actually compromised | | BPK and Bernese teachers' pension fund | Data theft came to light | Data categories not specified in the text |
This grid avoids two errors. The first is turning PKZH's worst-case scenario into a definitive list: the fund is still determining whether any data was stolen and, if so, which data. The second is treating the compromise of Posta's data as already established: the statement leaves precisely this question open.
The content of the categories makes the differences concrete. In PKZH's case, contact details, AVS, marital status, partner, IBAN, insured income and assets belong to different levels but appear in the same worst-case scenario. For Posta, on the other hand, the notice cites name, address, date of birth, AVS, contact details, email and pension data as potentially affected information. The overlap is not enough to say that the exposure is identical.
The technical point is also clear: the attack hit the external supplier, while PKZH's administrative system, which manages assets and pays out pensions, was apparently not affected. The source therefore does not report any interruption in pension payments. It describes an assessment of the scope of the data linked to the supplier.
For those monitoring their own pension position, the practical consequence is to read each communication by fund and category: confirmed data, possible data, benefits not at risk. Reports about BPK and the Bernese teachers' pension fund broaden the scope of the attack, but the text does not provide a total number of people involved or a common list for all institutions. ## How to navigate the available information The source allows for a reading procedure, not a standard request for all insured persons. The first criterion is to understand which pension institution is mentioned; the second is to distinguish what is confirmed from what remains to be verified.
### Four steps to avoid confusing statuses 1. **Identify the fund.** The statements concern PKZH and Posta's pension fund; the previous news item concerns BPK and the insurance fund for Bernese teachers. The status of one institution should not automatically be transferred to the others. 2. Separate what is confirmed from what is possible. For PKZH, investigations are still ongoing into the information stolen and the number of people affected. For Posta, it is not yet clear whether the insured persons' data were compromised. 3. Keep data and benefits separate. The personal and pension-related categories listed in the statements do not amount to a loss of assets. PKZH states that funds and annuity payments have not been affected; Posta says that assets and pension benefits are not at risk. 4. Recognize the formal actions already reported. PKZH has filed a criminal complaint and Posta has issued a statement about the attack. These are the official steps cited by the source; they do not by themselves establish which people are involved.
The text does not indicate a deadline for insured persons, a form, a request channel or an individual procedure to follow. Therefore, it is not possible to attribute to the source a date by which to submit an application or a definitive list of the data exposed. The questions still open are precise: PKZH must determine the information stolen and the number of people affected; for Posta, it must be clarified whether the insured persons' data have been compromised.
The most faithful reading, therefore, consists in not turning a list of the worst-case scenario into a complete confirmation and not confusing the attack on the provider with a risk to annuities. To learn more about the general topic of annuities, see rendite pensionistiche.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/attacco-informatico-a-casse-pensioni-citt%c3%a0-zurigo-e-posta/92224356)*

item.description: Guide to three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal - In Zurich, the municipal multiplier also matters - AFC/ESTV: direct federal tax and VAT - Online portal: tax rates, deductions and deadlines
## Key facts - Federal → IFD system, cantonal tax and municipal tax - AFC/ESTV → IFD and VAT - Cantonal administrations cantonal and municipal → taxes - Municipal multiplier → applied to cantonal tax - UST/BFS → statistics, not tax rates
In the Canton of Zurich, the analysis of cantonal and municipal taxes starts from the three-level structure of the Swiss tax authorities. The first is the direct federal tax; the other two are the cantonal level and the municipal level. The distinction is decisive when searching for rates, brackets, allowable deductions, delivery deadlines and the online portal of the cantonal tax administration.
Each Canton has its own law and its own multiplier. For municipalities, the multiplier is applied on the cantonal tax. Therefore, a study referring to Zurich should not be read as if there were only one tax item: the municipal component must be kept separate from the federal and cantonal ones.
### Who is competent
The institutional perimeter is equally important. The AFC/ESTV handles direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations, on the other hand, are the reference for cantonal and municipal taxes. The UFAS/BSV deals with social security, including AVS, AI and LPP, but does not set taxes. The UST/BFS produces statistics and does not establish rates.
This separation avoids using a statistical source to look up a tax percentage or confusing social security with tax reporting. For those who live in the Canton of Zurich, the correct route starts from the tax level concerned and then arrives at the official page relating to rates, brackets and deductions.
The online portal of the cantonal tax administration completes the operational framework indicated by the source. Its function, in practice, is to collect the information necessary for the delivery of the declaration and the verification of the applicable deadline. The municipal multiplier remains a separate step: it should not be replaced with the federal rate and should not be treated as a VAT item.
The same logic applies to the reading of the allowable deductions. First the tax level is identified, then the relevant cantonal or municipal rule is consulted. In this way, the cantonal tax research of the Canton of Zurich remains anchored to the correct competences, without attributing to the AFC/ESTV, the UFAS/BSV or the UST/BFS functions that they do not have. The practical calculation of the monthly burden and the tax return requires keeping three aspects separate: taxes, payroll contributions and the LAMal/KVG premium. They are different items, with distinct mechanisms and areas of responsibility. This distinction also helps to read a payslip correctly before looking for a tax deduction in the Canton of Zurich.
### Payslip and taxation
For payroll contributions, the source indicates that AVS/AI/IPG are 5,3% for the employee and 10,6% in total including the employer. AD/AC is 1,1% up to the annual maximum. For LAINF/LAA, the indicated figure ranges from 0,7% to 1,5% depending on the sector. LPP/BVG, calculated on the coordinated salary, provides for 7% between ages 25 and 34, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, and 18% from age 55 until the reference age.
These percentages describe social or insurance contributions on salary, not cantonal and municipal tax rates. A figure shown on the payslip therefore does not, by itself, make it possible to reconstruct the tax return calculation. Before assessing a deduction, it is necessary to identify the nature of the item and the tax level to which it relates.
| Item | Mechanism indicated by the source | |---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5,3% employee; 10,6% overall | | AD/AC | 1,1% up to the annual maximum | | LAINF/LAA | 0,7–1,5% depending on the sector | | LPP/BVG | Percentages on the coordinated salary by age bracket |
LAMal/KVG must also be excluded from the tax calculation. For residents, it is mandatory and must be taken out within three months of arrival. It is private, financed through per-capita premiums, and is neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. Premiums depend on the canton and the region, while the premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy.
This distinction has a concrete effect on the household budget and the cost of living: the health-insurance premium should not be presented as a tax rate, and a social-security withholding should not be confused with the municipal multiplier. To understand Zurich's framework, it is therefore necessary to separate the calculation of direct federal tax, the cantonal and municipal tax calculations, payroll contributions and LAMal premiums. To properly consult cantonal and municipal taxes in the Canton of Zurich, it is advisable to follow a fixed sequence. The procedure avoids looking for a percentage in the wrong place and keeps separate rates, steps, deductions and deadlines.
### Five-step procedure
1. **Identify the tax level.** Indicates whether the verification concerns direct federal tax, cantonal tax or municipal tax. If VAT appears, the reference is the AFC/ESTV; for cantonal and municipal taxes, the reference is the cantonal administrations.
2. Open the cantonal portal. Use the online portal of the cantonal tax administration to search for information related to the Canton of Zurich. The consultation must cover the rates, the steps, the allowable deductions and the deadline for delivery of the declaration.
3. Check the municipal multiplier. The municipality applies the multiplier on the cantonal tax. This figure must therefore be read separately from the federal component and the cantonal base, without replacing it with a paycheck item or with VAT.
4. Check the reference year. The source reports that some figures are indexed every year. The control concerns, among others, the third pillar 3a ceiling, the LPP coordination threshold or deduction, the AD/AC ceiling, the average LAMal premiums and the median salary. It is not advisable to automatically transfer an amount from one year to the next.
5. Separate pension and health insurance. AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA and LPP/BVG are salary contributions. LAMal is instead a mandatory insurance for residents, with per capita premiums and cantonal premium reductions. If a person has just arrived in Switzerland, the stipulation must be made within three months of arrival.
For an orderly check, note the tax level, municipality, multiplier, deduction considered, and term displayed on the portal. If the data concerns statistics, the UST/BFS is not the source for setting rates. If it concerns social security, the UFAS/BSV is not the office that determines taxes. To proceed to compilation, open dichiarazione delle imposte.

item.title: Swiss health system: LAMal 2026 guide in the canton of Zurich
item.description: Practical guide to the health system in the canton of Zurich for 2026: LAMal obligations, choice of cash, deductibles and reimbursement procedures for residents.

## TL;DR - LAMal is the mandatory health insurance for every resident. - Coverage must be taken out within three months of arrival in Switzerland. - The premiums vary according to the canton of residence and the deductible chosen. - The reduction of premiums is managed through specific cantonal subsidies.
## Key facts - Insurance obligation: Within 3 months of arrival - Adult deductibles: CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 - Rewards management: Per capita - Level of competence: Cantonal and Federal
The Swiss healthcare system is regulated by the Federal Health Insurance Act (KVG). For every individual residing in the canton of Zurich, as in the rest of the Confederation, there is an obligation to take out basic insurance coverage within three months of establishing their official residence. This insurance is private in nature, but the benefits covered are standardized at the federal level to ensure equitable access to necessary medical care. The monthly premium, which each insured must pay, does not constitute a tax, but a fixed cost which varies depending on the place of residence, age and the selected deductible. In the canton of Zurich, the competent authorities monitor the application of the legislation and manage the procedures relating to subsidies for the reduction of premiums, a fundamental mechanism for supporting sections of the population with lower incomes. It is important to underline that the KVG does not depend on the salary or the employer, unlike other social coverage such as the AVS/AHV or the LPP/BVG, which are strictly linked to the job position and the salary contributions paid. The choice of health insurance company is entirely up to the citizen, who can compare the different offers on the market, while being aware that the basic benefits are identical by law in each insurance company. The federal administration, through the FOPH/BAG, defines the regulatory framework, while the cantons retain operational responsibility for correct implementation and support for families. The structure of the system is based on a clear separation between the management of premiums, which is private, and regulation, which remains public, thus ensuring that the quality of medical care remains high throughout the country.
### The structure of the basic covers Every KVG contract obligatorily includes basic benefits, which cover the costs of diagnosis, treatment, hospitalization and prescribed drugs. The distinction between the different health insurance companies lies mainly in customer service, in the speed of reimbursement and in the variety of alternative insurance models (such as the family doctor or Telmed model), which allow you to obtain discounts on premiums with a limitation in the immediate choice of a specialist doctor. Transparency in the system is guaranteed by constant vigilance, ensuring that no citizen is rejected for underlying health reasons. A practical analysis of the system in the canton of Zurich requires a clear understanding of the cost dynamics and the benefits available to residents. Unlike other European systems, Switzerland adopts a model based on fixed per-capita premiums, independent of income or assets. This feature makes individual financial planning essential. In the canton of Zurich, citizens have the option to choose between different deductibles, which represent the annual amount the insured pays out-of-pocket before the health insurance fund begins to cover medical costs. Authorized deductibles for adults start at 300 francs and go up to a maximum of 2500 francs. Opting for a higher deductible allows for a significant reduction in the monthly premium, but exposes the individual to greater financial risk in the event of frequent medical needs. This is a calculation that every resident must perform based on their own health status and current economic availability. In addition to the deductible, the insured contributes to costs through a percentage co-payment (usually 10%) once the deductible is reached, as well as a daily contribution for hospital stays. The canton of Zurich offers a premium reduction system (subsidies) that helps relieve families and individuals within certain income brackets. The procedure for requesting such a subsidy must be followed strictly according to the deadlines set by the cantonal authority. It is not uncommon for residents to underestimate the impact of these decisions on their household budget management. Comparing different insurance models is facilitated by the availability of official portals and calculation tools that allow users to view the offers available for 2026. The stability of the Swiss system is supported by the financial soundness of health insurance funds, which are subject to strict federal regulations that prevent speculation and ensure solvency. For those who have recently moved, it is essential not to wait until the last day of the three-month registration period to avoid administrative complications or periods of non-coverage that could lead to unexpected costs for the insured. Planning must also include checking supplementary coverage, which, while not mandatory, can complement the LAMal for extra services such as private room stays or specific dental treatments.
### Risk management and savings Careful management of one's insurance position is a fundamental skill for those living in Zurich. The optimization strategy involves choosing the correct insurance model. For those in good health, models such as Telmed allow for the reduction of fixed costs. However, it is necessary to carefully evaluate whether the flexibility required in case of emergency is compatible with one's personal needs. Financial planning should always consider the deductible amount as a fixed expense set aside, ensuring the necessary liquidity to cover unforeseen medical expenses during the fiscal year. To activate or modify your insurance coverage in the canton of Zurich, the procedure requires a few precise steps. First, it is necessary to compare the updated offers for 2026 using the official comparators recognized by the federal administration. Once you have selected the health insurance fund that best meets your needs, enrollment is completed by signing a health insurance contract. It is essential to keep a copy of the policy and the documents sent, as these constitute proof of coverage in accordance with the law. If you are already a resident, changing your health insurance fund is possible within the established deadlines, which usually require the cancellation of the previous contract by the end of November for the following year. Regarding the request for premium reductions, the citizen must submit an application to the competent cantonal offices, providing the necessary documentation attesting to their income situation. Often, the canton of Zurich sends the necessary forms ex officio to those who meet the criteria, but it is the citizen's responsibility to verify the correct receipt and timely submission of the documents. If needed, the cantonal portal offers detailed guides and direct contacts with the relevant offices. Another aspect to monitor is the updating of your personal data with the insurance fund; any change of address or civil status must be communicated promptly to avoid errors in premium billing. Reimbursements for medical expenses (invoices paid directly by the insured) must be sent to the health insurance fund within the prescribed limitation periods, usually accompanied by the original documentation issued by the healthcare provider. Remember to always use the official cantonal portal to check the updated requirements for 2026, as subsidy regulations may vary based on the decisions of the Grand Council. Proper management of these obligations ensures not only compliance with the law but also efficient management of your household budget, avoiding penalties or loss of subsidies. For those wishing to learn more about financial protection options and health planning, it is recommended to consult the tools available on the site. item.title: Former Credit Suisse executives, cancellation of bonuses confirmed
item.description: The TF confirms the revocation of bonuses for former CS executives The TAF had upheld the appeals in March 2025 Bonus cuts: 100%, 50% and 25% for three levels The 19th
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The TF confirms the revocation of bonuses for former CS executives - The TAF had upheld the appeals in March 2025 - Bonus cuts: 100%, 50% and 25% for three levels - The acquisition of CS by UBS was announced on March 19, 2023
## Key facts - What → revocation of variable compensation not yet paid - Authority → TF, following the appeal by the Confederation and UBS - Rule → Article 10a of the Banking Act (LBCR) - Measures → 100%, 50% and 25% at the three highest management levels - Average reduction → 68'000 francs - Liquidity assistance → 168 billion francs, fully repaid
LAUSANNE - The Federal Supreme Court (TF) declared the revocation of bonuses awarded to former Credit Suisse (CS) executives lawful, overturning the decision of the Federal Administrative Court (TAF) and upholding the appeal by the Confederation and UBS. The ruling concerns variable compensation intended for the three highest management levels of the now-defunct institution, but not yet paid.
At the center was Article 10a of the Banking Act (LBCR). The TF had to determine whether this provision was sufficient to allow the Federal Council to revoke in whole or in part remuneration still to be paid when a systemically important bank, or its parent company, receives direct or indirect state aid using Confederation funds.
The appeals by the affected executives had been upheld by the TAF in March 2025. The lower court held that the provision permitted only temporary measures, namely suspension of payment. In its judgment of September 16, published today, the TF instead adopted a different interpretation.
### The interpretation of Article 10a
For the judges in Lausanne, the duration of the support referred to by the law indicates the period during which the government is authorized to issue measures, not the duration of the individual measure. Moreover, the fact that the right to variable remuneration may be “limited” indicates something more than simply postponing payment.
The TF also referred to the Federal Council’s message to Parliament on the amendment of the LBCR and the introduction of the too big to fail rules. In that document, according to the judgment, the government specified that the measures could go as far as revoking variable remuneration and affect the related rights.
The aim was to prevent public funds from financing bonuses deemed inappropriate, including those contractually provided for but not yet paid for previous financial years. The TF found that the conditions of Article 10a had been met and held that the Federal Council was required to take measures. The reduction was applied gradually: 100% at the first management level, 50% at the second and 25% at the third. On average, the cut reached 68'000 francs, while fixed remuneration in the final year of employment, which was not reduced, was approximately 1,4 million. ## What changes for the case under review
The practical difference between the two judgments concerns the meaning of the measure adopted by the Federal Council. The TAF had interpreted it as a temporary suspension: payment of variable compensation would be deferred. The TF, however, held that the word «limited» also allows for a substantial reduction or a total or partial revocation of bonuses not yet paid.
### Three levels, three measures
| Management level | Reduction applied to bonuses | |---|---:| | First level | 100% | | Second level | 50% | | Third level | 25% |
The case therefore does not involve a uniform cut for all those affected. The percentage depends on the management level: 100% indicates the largest measure, while 25% is the smallest among those indicated in the source. The economic comparison provided by the judges adds two points of reference: the average reduction was 68'000 francs and, in the last year of employment, the average unreduced fixed remuneration was approximately 1,4 million francs.
For anyone interpreting variable remuneration in the Credit Suisse case, the distinction between the fixed component and bonuses is therefore decisive. The ruling concerns variable compensation not yet paid; according to the data reported by the Federal Supreme Court, fixed remuneration was not reduced. The source also specifies that contractually stipulated variable remuneration for previous financial years could be involved, when the foundations for the need for state aid had been laid.
The judges rejected the executives' argument that the decision was a sanction. Article 10a, in the TF's interpretation, serves preventive rather than punitive purposes. The employees had been informed of the possibility of eliminating the variable component through restrictive clauses included in their compensation plans.
The scope of the decision remains as described by the source: direct or indirect state aid using Confederation funds to a systemically important bank or its parent company. The measures apply during the period in which the government is authorized to intervene. The judgment therefore does not turn every salary dispute into a similar issue: the TF's reasoning is tied to the provision, public support and the three management levels in the CS case. ## How to reconstruct the case
The sequence of events makes it possible to verify why the issue of bonuses was linked to the liquidity crisis and the intervention of the Confederation. To follow the case without confusing the different stages, it is advisable to proceed by date and distinguish the authorities' announcements from the judicial decisions.
### The institutional sequence
1. On March 15, 2023, FINMA and BNS announced that Credit Suisse continued to meet capital and liquidity requirements. At the same time, BNS announced liquidity support.
2. On March 16, the Federal Council issued the liquidity support ordinance. This provided for additional loans and Confederation guarantees in the event of default for loans granted by BNS to systemically important banks.
3. On March 19, 2023, UBS's acquisition of CS was announced. On the same day, the Federal Council amended the ordinance on liquidity assistance, adding a provision on the adoption of measures concerning remuneration.
4. By the end of March 2023, CS had received liquidity assistance amounting to 168 billion francs; the amount was repaid in full.
5. Only after reconstructing this sequence can one examine the judicial stage: in March 2025, TAF had upheld the appeals, while TF subsequently overturned that decision in the judgment of September 16 published today.
To correctly apply the logic of the case, there are three points to check: the remuneration must be variable and not yet paid; the measure must concern one of the three highest management levels; the legal reference is Article 10a of LBCR, linked to the public support provided for by law. The scale indicated by the judges remains 100%, 50% and 25%, not a single percentage for everyone.
The source does not describe an individual procedure, a form or a deadline for other workers. Therefore, the case should be read as a federal decision on the remuneration of former CS executives, without automatically extending its effects to different situations. To connect the distinction between fixed and variable pay with reading your own payslip, consult busta paga svizzera.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/economia/1956910/federale-cs-misure-consiglio-articolo-liquidita-marzo-confederazione-bonus-dirigenti)*

item.title: Secondhand markets: warranty, sidewalk and counterfeit goods across the border
item.description: Used: one-year warranty, unless explicitly excluded «Sold as seen» excludes the warranty Free items on public land: often prohibited Fakes
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Used item: one-year warranty, unless explicitly excluded - «Sold as seen» excludes the warranty - Free items on public land: often prohibited - Counterfeits from abroad: seizure and approximately 100 francs ## Key facts - Guarantee at a flea market → one year, unless excluded - Receipt → at least the seller's details - Public space → no general right to distribute for free - Private land → gifts generally permitted - Counterfeits from abroad → possible seizure and a fee of about 100 francs - Returns and exchanges → granted only voluntarily Gabriela Baumgartner's explanations (Radio SRF 1, October 5, 2026) start from a concrete misconception: an item with the word «free» written on the sidewalk is not automatically a lawful gift. The market also includes flea markets, second-hand shops and online platforms. ### Public space and private land In many municipalities, leaving boxes containing books, furniture or other items on the sidewalk or along the road may be considered illegal waste disposal and, when it takes place on public land, is often prohibited. There is no general right to distribute goods for free while occupying public space. Some cities apply strict rules, while others tolerate the practice as long as the passage remains clear and the items are removed promptly. On private land, it is generally permitted to leave items intended to be given away: by making them available, the original owner relinquishes ownership and whoever collects them becomes their lawful owner. Excluded are bags from official used-clothing collections, which remain the property of the sponsoring organization. The provisions of the Code of Obligations also apply to purchases made at flea markets. In principle, anyone who buys a used item benefits from a one-year warranty. The seller may exclude it: «sold as seen» is an explicit exclusion, and the buyer waives the related rights. A receipt containing at least the seller's details makes it possible to identify who sold the goods in the event of disputes. The sale of stolen goods or counterfeit articles constitutes a criminal offense. Someone who buys a product of this type in good faith at a flea market in Switzerland does not, however, commit a criminal offense. If the purchase takes place abroad, counterfeit branded products may be seized, and anyone who brings them into Switzerland risks a fee of about 100 francs. In second-hand shops, the warranty provided for second-hand goods lasts one year instead of two and may be excluded if the customer is clearly informed. Swiss law does not provide for a general right of withdrawal: returns and exchanges depend on the seller's willingness. ## A used item does not always follow the same rule The practical distinction concerns the location, the type of seller, and the condition attached to the purchase. A box left in the street is subject to different rules from an item displayed on private property. Likewise, a flea market and a second-hand shop have warranties of similar duration, but the latter is a commercial establishment in every respect. ### Four useful comparisons | Situation | Consequence indicated by the source | |---|---| | Public land | The gift may be prohibited or considered illegal disposal | | Private land | The gift is generally permitted and ownership passes to whoever takes the item | | Flea market in Switzerland | One-year warranty, unless excluded; a good-faith buyer does not commit a criminal offense | | Second-hand shop | One-year warranty instead of two, with possible clear exclusion | | Cross-border purchase | Counterfeit branded products may be seized and entail a fee of approximately 100 francs | The first comparison shows that price is not the only factor to consider. Before even asking whether an item is a good deal, whoever offers it free of charge must consider whether it is on public land or private property. The consequence may be that the practice is prohibited or that ownership passes to whoever picks up the item. The second concerns the warranty. At a flea market, the buyer is entitled, in principle, to a one-year warranty, but may lose it by accepting a formula such as «sold as seen». In a second-hand shop, the period is one year instead of two, and exclusion is possible when the customer is informed clearly. The duration of the warranty, however, does not create a general right to return the goods: Swiss law does not require the seller to take back a purchase made in error. The exceptionally low price then requires a separate assessment. If a genuine designer bag is offered well below market value, the buyer may purchase it without informing the seller of its real value. The seller may, however, challenge the contract if he proves that he sold the item without knowing its value. Finally, the risk linked to the border changes. A good-faith purchase at a Swiss flea market does not constitute a criminal offense for the buyer. For purchases in neighboring countries, however, customs checks on counterfeit branded products can lead to seizure and a demand for a fee of approximately 100 francs. ## Before closing the deal ### Five practical steps 1. If you want to give an item away, check where you are leaving it. Sidewalks and streets are public spaces: in many municipalities, this practice is prohibited and may be considered illegal waste disposal. On private property, it is generally permitted. Bags used for official collections of used clothing, on the other hand, remain the property of the organization promoting the collection. 2. Before buying, carefully check the condition of the item. Ask the seller questions and ask yourself whether the price is plausible. When it appears exceptionally advantageous, the source urges caution; if you decide to proceed anyway, ask for a receipt. 3. At the flea market, have at least the seller’s details included on the receipt. In the event of a subsequent dispute, this makes it possible to identify who sold the goods. Also check whether there are clauses excluding the warranty: “sold as seen” has this effect. 4. In a second-hand shop, ask what warranty comes with the item. For second-hand goods, it lasts one year instead of two, but the retailer may exclude it if they clearly inform the customer. Do not take an exchange for granted: returns and replacements are voluntary. 5. If you buy in neighboring countries and the item is branded, pay particular attention to the risk of counterfeiting. Customs authorities may seize the product, and anyone bringing it into Switzerland risks a fee of around 100 francs. The buyer’s good faith excludes criminal liability for a flea-market purchase in Switzerland, but does not eliminate the stated risk when returning from abroad. After the sale or purchase, do not confuse the warranty with the right of withdrawal: the latter is not general. If the purchase turns out to be a mistake, the seller is not required to take the goods back, unless they voluntarily choose to offer a return or exchange. To compare exchange rates for cross-border purchases, consult the comparatore CHF/EUR. *Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/info/dialogo/Mercatini-e-usato-cinque-cose-da-sapere--4155286.html)*

item.title: Cyberattack hits Zurich’s pension fund
item.description: PKZH personal data stolen in an attack on a software provider Pension funds and annuities were not affected The attack dates back to the end of September
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - PKZH personal data stolen in an attack on a software provider - Pension assets and pension payments were not affected - The attack dates back to the end of September - PKZH filed a criminal complaint
## Key facts - Fund: PKZH, the pension fund of the City of Zurich - Attack: against an external software provider - When: at the end of September - Worst-case scenario: contact details, AVS, IBAN and pension data - Effects: pension assets and pension payments unaffected - Administrative system: reportedly not affected - Action: criminal complaint filed by PKZH - Verification: stolen data and affected people still to be determined
On Thursday, PKZH, the pension fund of the City of Zurich, announced that personal data of its insured members had been stolen. The cyberattack targeted an external software provider, without affecting pension assets or pension payments. The statement thus distinguishes the theft of information from the payment of benefits.
The cyberattack dates back to the end of September. Since a switch to a new management system was planned, the fund had already sent its data to the company. PKZH filed a criminal complaint. In the meantime, it is trying to determine precisely what information was stolen and how many people were affected.
### Reconstructing the attack
The worst-case scenario listed by the fund includes personal contact details: name, address, email and telephone number. The same list includes the AVS number, marital status, information about partners, the IBAN number and pension data such as insured income and assets. The wording is conditional: the source does not present these categories as a list already confirmed for every person.
According to the statement, the administrative system used by PKZH to manage assets and pay pensions does not appear to have been involved in the attack. For the fund’s operations, this is therefore the limit indicated by the source. What remains unresolved, however, is reconstructing the full set of copied data and determining the number of insured members affected.
The case follows announcements from other Swiss pension funds. In the preceding days, other funds, including the public-sector fund in Bern, had announced that they had fallen victim to the cyberattack. The text does not specify which data were involved in the Bern case.
On Thursday, possible involvement by the Posta pension fund had also been raised. The source clarifies that this has not been established. Warnings appeared on its website, but this does not turn the hypothesis into a confirmation. The PKZH statement, by contrast, explicitly links the transmission of the data to the new management system project and the breach at the external provider. ## The practical implications for insured persons
For those who live or work in Switzerland and are insured with PKZH, the news has two distinct aspects: continuity of pension provision and the confidentiality of information. Regarding the former, the fund says that assets and pension payments have not been affected; the administrative system used to manage assets and pay benefits would also not have been affected. Regarding the latter, the potential leak concerns more than mere contact details, because the worst-case scenario includes an AHV number, an IBAN and pension data. The source does not report any money transfers or a suspension of pension payments. The available information concerns the theft of information.
### What is certain and what remains open
| Point | Confirmed or reported | Still to be clarified | |---|---|---| | Personal data | PKZH has reported a data theft | Which categories were actually taken | | People affected | The fund is determining the number | How many | | Assets and pensions | Funds and payments have not been affected | The complete analysis at the provider | | Posta's pension fund | Involvement not established | Possible confirmation |
The transition to a new management system explains why the data were held by an external company: the source says that they had been transmitted before the attack. It does not say that the system PKZH uses to manage assets and pay benefits was hit. For readers, this distinction prevents confusing a data leak with a change in pension benefits.
The reference to the other funds should also be read carefully. The Bernese public pension fund had already stated that it had fallen victim to the cyberattack, but the text does not automatically attribute the same categories of data to that case. As for Posta's pension fund, however, its involvement remains unconfirmed, despite the warnings that appeared on the website. Until PKZH completes its investigation, the number of people affected and the actual list of information stolen remain the two decisive elements. ## How to follow the case without confusing the notices
The source does not describe an individual procedure involving forms, deadlines or numbers to call. It does, however, offer a sequence of checks that avoids premature conclusions.
### Four steps based on the communication
1. Separate the funds involved. The confirmed case concerns PKZH. The Bernese public fund is mentioned as an already announced victim; Posta appears only with unconfirmed involvement and warnings on the website.
2. Treat the list of data as a worst-case scenario, not as individual confirmation. PKZH is verifying which information was stolen and how many people are involved.
3. Keep data and benefits separate. The communication states that pension funds and pension payments were not affected and that the administrative system would not have been affected.
4. Record the only formal act indicated: PKZH has filed a criminal complaint. This is the procedural step reported by the source; no other requirements for insured persons are described.
This scope makes it possible not to attribute instructions to the source that it does not contain. No deadline by which insured persons must respond, method of individual notification, document to send or dedicated channel is indicated. The news therefore does not make it possible to set a personal deadline.
The next verifiable element will be the outcome of the analysis launched by PKZH: which data were actually stolen and how many people are involved. Until then, the most precise distinction remains this: data theft confirmed, scope still to be determined, benefits unaffected according to the communication.
For more information about pensions, use strumento AVS/LPP/rendita.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4167841)*

item.title: RUAG and Lockheed Martin agreement for three F-35As in Emmen
item.description: RUAG MRO and Lockheed Martin continue the RIGI project Three F-35As will be assembled at the RUAG facility in Emmen The first components are expected in the first half
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR
- RUAG MRO and Lockheed Martin continue the RIGI project - Three F-35A aircraft will be assembled at the RUAG site in Emmen - The first components are expected in the first half of 2027 - Production will start in autumn 2027
## Key facts
- Agreement → RUAG MRO and Lockheed Martin - Project → RIGI - Aircraft → three F-35A - Initial plan → four planes - Headquarters → Emmen (LU) - Components → first half of 2027 - Production → autumn 2027 - Locations worldwide → four for final assembly and testing
RUAG MRO and Lockheed Martin have signed an agreement to continue the cooperation in the framework of the RIGI project. The program involves the assembly of three F-35A fighter aircraft at the RUAG headquarters in Emmen (LU), destined to become one of only four locations in the world for the final assembly and testing of the fighters.
### The industrial calendar
The agreement opens a new phase of the project and will allow Switzerland to acquire skills for future aircraft maintenance. The arrival of the first components in Switzerland is expected in the first half of 2027; production is expected to begin in the autumn of the same year. RUAG, a company owned by the Confederation, indicated these steps in a note.
The initial plan included four planes. In detailed planning, the number was reduced to three to adapt the program to the requirements and available resources. Planning therefore reduces the expected size of the assembly; in the same initiative, RUAG indicates the acquisition of know-how as one of the objectives of the project.
According to RUAG, the project will allow Switzerland to acquire know-how on the F-35A, a new generation fighter, and increase national autonomy in maintenance activities. The company also aims to equip itself with the skills to offer the Swiss Army comprehensive support for the entire operational life of the fighters in the future.
The project also aims to support regional employment and consolidate RUAG as a European center of competence in military aviation. In this framework, the initiative combines the acquisition of technical capabilities, support for maintenance and strengthening of the industrial role. In the press release, Jürg Rötheli, chairman of the board of directors of RUAG MRO Holding SA, underlined its strategic value for the future of the company. He also highlighted that participation in the F-35A program aims to contribute to Switzerland's security and defense capability. ## What it means for Switzerland
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the significance of the project lies not only in assembling three aircraft in Emmen. The new development concerns the type of expertise RUAG intends to build around the F-35A: final assembly, testing, knowledge of the aircraft and future maintenance. The Emmen site will become one of only four sites worldwide for the two main operational activities, a position that RUAG links to consolidating its role as a European center of expertise in military aviation.
### Comparison with the initial plan
The first practical point is the change from four to three aircraft. The initial plan called for four aircraft; detailed planning reduced the number to align the program with the requirements and available resources. The updated figure is therefore three. The number four describes the initial setup, while three is the reference figure for the project in its detailed planning.
| Item | Information from the source | Practical interpretation | |---|---|---| | Aircraft | Four in the initial plan; three in the detailed planning | The updated reference is three | | Site | Emmen (LU), RUAG site | One of only four sites worldwide for final assembly and testing | | Expertise | Know-how and autonomy in maintenance | Capabilities to be acquired and strengthened | | Support | Full support for the Swiss Armed Forces | Future objective |
The second point is maintenance. The objective is not limited to the assembly phase: RUAG refers to know-how about the aircraft and Swiss autonomy in maintenance. The company also wants to develop the expertise needed to ensure full support for the Swiss Armed Forces in the future throughout the entire life cycle of the F-35As. The source therefore describes a process of acquiring and developing capabilities; it does not present full support as an activity that has already been completed.
The third point concerns employment. According to RUAG, the initiative will help secure jobs at the regional level. The source does not assign a number of hires to this objective or indicate job profiles. The employment impact is stated as a regional contribution, while the industrial value is linked to strengthening RUAG as a European center of expertise. ## How to follow the project
To follow the project in a concrete way, it is useful to separate what has been signed, what has been scheduled and what RUAG intends to develop. This sequence makes it possible to read the updates without confusing the start of the collaboration with the start of production or future objectives with results already achieved.
### Four operational checks
1. Agreement. The starting point is the signing between RUAG MRO and Lockheed Martin to continue the collaboration on the RIGI project. It is the step that opens the new phase described by the company.
2. Quantity. The updated reference is three F-35A for assembly in Emmen (LU). The number four belongs to the initial plan; detailed planning adopted three aircraft, taking requirements and available resources into consideration.
3. Calendar. The first deadline to observe is the arrival of the components in the first half of 2027. The second is the start of production in the autumn of the same year. These are two different moments: the first concerns the availability of the components, the second the beginning of production.
4. Results. The acquisition of know-how, Switzerland's autonomy in maintenance, full support for the Swiss Army and the contribution to regional jobs fall under the objectives and effects declared by RUAG. They should be read according to the verbs used by the company: acquire, strengthen, develop and contribute.
### A useful criterion for the Swiss reader
Every future update can be compared with three indicators drawn from the source. The first concerns the site: Emmen will become one of only four sites in the world for final assembly and testing. The second concerns expertise: RUAG wants to acquire know-how about the aircraft and strengthen Switzerland's autonomy in maintenance. The third concerns the company's outlook: the company intends to provide full support to the Swiss Army throughout the F-35A life cycle and consolidate its European role.
Communication about employment should also be read precisely. RUAG links the initiative to the guarantee of jobs at the regional level, but does not provide a number. Therefore, it is more accurate to distinguish between industrial objectives, skills to be developed and completed results.
To get an overview of the employment side of the Swiss market, one can consult aziende che assumono, keeping the general search separate from the specific information on the RIGI project.
