## TL;DR - The referendum on the law is scheduled for November 29 - 36 Western countries would have greater freedom to purchase - The Federal Council would retain a veto over neutrality - Supporters link the revision to technology and jobs
## Key facts - Vote → 29 November - Countries concerned → 36 Western countries - Veto → Federal Council - Exclusion → States with serious and systematic human rights violations - Campaign → Swiss Security Alliance and Swiss Employers' Association - Re-export → Ukraine excluded
The vote on the weapons law, against which a referendum has been launched, is scheduled for 29 November. A coalition of representatives of the UDC, the PLR, the Centre and the Green Liberals supports its approval. According to the proponents, without more flexible rules for the export of war materiel, Switzerland would risk losing the technologies and know-how needed for its own defence.
The new framework would allow 36 Western countries to purchase Swiss arms with greater freedom than today, even if they were involved in a war. Nations that seriously and systematically violate human rights would remain excluded. The Federal Council would have a right of veto, for example if it deemed the exports dangerous to neutrality. As regards re-export, in principle all countries could transfer to third parties the material purchased in Switzerland; Ukraine is excluded. The Federal Council could require a guarantee that it would remain in the purchasing country if there were doubts about Swiss neutrality or Swiss foreign and security policy.
### The supporters' campaign
The campaign in favour of the revision is being conducted under the auspices of the Swiss Security Alliance and the Swiss Employers' Association. The proponents argue that the rules should be made more flexible in light of developments in the international situation.
> National Councillor Reto Nause (Centre/BE) told the media today that «Parliament amended the War Material Act because we are facing the stark reality of a world at war.»
Nause argued that Switzerland should remain integrated into the international value chain in order to procure war materiel and preserve expertise useful for defence. Michael Götte (UDC/SG) referred to the veto linked to neutrality and argued that the revision would strengthen it rather than weaken it.
Monika Rühl, director of Economiesuisse, warned that a no vote could put numerous jobs at risk: the relocation of companies abroad would also eliminate apprenticeships in the technology sector and highly qualified jobs. Sidney Kamerzin (Centre/VS) clarified that the new rules would not constitute an unconditional authorisation: states that systematically violate human rights or use weapons against their own civilian population would continue not to receive supplies. The checks, he added, would remain in place, but would be shifted from the time of the conflict to the time of purchase. ## The repercussions for the Swiss supply chain
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the issue described by the source hinges above all on three connected elements: the ability to export, the continuity of the technology industry and the ability to support defense. The issue is not only how many weapons can be sold, but when Switzerland exercises control and how much leeway it gives purchasing countries.
### Before and after: when control is exercised
| Point | Situation described today | Proposed approach | |---|---|---| | Purchase in wartime | A neighboring country or partner under attack no longer receives Swiss ammunition or spare parts. | The 36 Western countries can purchase with greater freedom even if they are involved in a war. | | Re-export | What a country has bought from Switzerland cannot be transferred to its allies. | In principle, the material can be transferred to third parties; Ukraine is excluded, and the Federal Council may request a guarantee. | | Control | According to Michael Götte, today the decision is made only when a conflict breaks out, with international and media pressure already in place. | Control shifts to the time of sale, with the Federal Council having veto power. |
The comparison highlights the risk identified by the Alliance: rejecting the new rules could weaken the industrial base that supports the defense system. Monika Rühl links a possible relocation of companies abroad to the loss of apprenticeships and highly skilled jobs. Vaud National Councillor Céline Weber adds that, in recent years, several companies specializing in research and development have moved their headquarters abroad; start-ups and spin-offs in artificial intelligence, drones and information technology have been founded directly outside Switzerland.
The issue also affects military planning. Heinz Theiler, a PLR member from Schwyz in the National Council, has deemed it imprudent to invest billions in the army while simultaneously leaving the industry that keeps those systems running in crisis. His argument therefore links export policy to the future availability of technology and expertise, not just to arms sales.
For Swiss residents, the practical effect identified by the supporters is indirect but concrete: a choice about export rules can affect whether industrial activities, research, apprenticeships and skilled jobs remain in Switzerland. The source attributes this assessment to the revision's supporters. ## How to assess the choice before November 29
The source makes it possible to turn the discussion into an orderly assessment, without confusing export, re-export and neutrality. To form an opinion on the vote, the process can follow five steps.
1. Identify the subject. The referendum concerns the Weapons Act and the revision of the rules for war materiel. The date indicated is the vote on November 29. 2. Separate the recipients. The greater freedom to purchase is not described as applying to the whole world: it concerns a group of 36 Western countries. The proposal excludes nations responsible for serious and systematic human rights violations. 3. Distinguish between purchase and transfer. Even if all countries would, in principle, have the possibility of transferring to third parties the armaments bought in Switzerland, Ukraine remains excluded under the framework reported by the source. 4. Verify the role of the Federal Council. The point to examine is its power of veto at the time of sale. In the event of doubts about neutrality or foreign and security policy interests, the Federal Council could also request a guarantee that the material remain in the purchasing country. 5. Compare the consequences. On the one hand, there are the Alliance’s reasons: maintaining technologies, know-how, companies, apprenticeships and skilled jobs in Switzerland. On the other, there is the political question of neutrality and the limits to be maintained, to which the proponents respond by invoking the veto and oversight.
### Two scenarios to keep separate
With approval, the framework described by the new approach would open greater possibilities for sales to the 36 Western countries and make re-export more flexible, while still leaving the Federal Council tools for intervention. With rejection, the current rules described in the source would remain: a neighboring country or an attacked partner would no longer receive Swiss ammunition or spare parts and could not transfer to its allies what it had purchased. Supporters also warn that a no vote would put technologies, know-how, jobs and apprenticeships at risk.
To follow the employment dimension of the discussion, consult annunci di lavoro.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/export-armi-importante-per-sicurezza-della-svizzera/92222311)*

## TL;DR - Parmelin meets Charnvirakul in Bangkok on October 15, 2026 - Switzerland and Thailand are pursuing the EFTA free trade agreement - The visit to Vietnam continues on October 17, 2026 - The EFTA-Vietnam signing is scheduled for October 18, 2026
## Key facts - What → bilateral talks and free trade agreement - Location → Bangkok - Date → October 15, 2026 - Switzerland → Guy Parmelin - Thailand → Anutin Charnvirakul - Next stop → Vietnam - Reception in Hanoi → October 17, 2026 - Signing of the EFTA-Vietnam agreement → October 18, 2026
On October 15, 2026, in Bangkok, President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin met with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul during his official visit to Thailand. The discussions covered bilateral relations, negotiations for the free trade agreement between Thailand and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and key international issues.
### A 95-year relationship 95 years have passed since diplomatic relations were established between Switzerland and Thailand. During the meeting, both sides expressed satisfaction with their political, economic and civil society relations. The community of Swiss citizens abroad in Thailand numbers over 13 000 people and is the largest in the Asia-Pacific region; 30 000 Thai citizens live in Switzerland.
### Free trade at the centre The two interlocutors emphasized the importance of the EFTA-Thailand agreement for the further development of bilateral economic relations. Parmelin and Charnvirakul discussed the steps leading up to its entry into force and how best to take advantage of the opportunities. The discussions highlighted the potential of manufacturing and automation, digital technologies, infrastructure and sustainable technologies.
The President of the Swiss Confederation also expressed Switzerland’s interest in investing in Thailand as part of cooperation on climate change under Article 6 of the Climate Agreement. The stated objective is to support measures aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
### The The topics discussed included the impact of the international situation on regional stability, the reform of the World Trade Organization (WTO), the United Nations and the role of International Geneva as a hub of multilateral diplomacy. Parmelin also acknowledged Thailand’s efforts to combat criminal networks on the internet.
### The stop in Vietnam The presidential mission will continue in Vietnam, where President of the Swiss Confederation Parmelin will be received in Hanoi by President Tô Lâm on October 17, 2026. The agenda includes meetings with Prime Minister Lê Minh Hưng, President of the National Assembly Trần Thanh Mẫne and other government representatives. A Swiss business delegation will accompany the President on both legs of the trip, in Thailand and Vietnam. For a Swiss reader, the impact described is an economic prospect, not an operational result that is already available. The communiqué refers to an EFTA-Thailand agreement to be guided toward entry into force and to opportunities to be seized. The distinction separates the political dialogue from the subsequent phase. The text does not specify products, procedures, economic values, or a date for entry into force; it therefore does not allow savings or obligations already in force to be attributed.
### A map, not a list of contracts Production and automation are identified as a first area of potential. For a Swiss operator, the reference helps identify which part of the dossier to follow, but it does not certify orders, investments, or agreements already concluded. Digital technologies form a second pillar; infrastructure and sustainable technologies complete the list. The communiqué does not link these sectors to a company, a project, or an implementation schedule. The practical implication is to distinguish an area of interest from a result already obtained.
The link to climate points in a specific direction. Parmelin has expressed Switzerland’s interest in investing in Thailand in projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, under Article 6 of the Climate Agreement. The environmental dimension accompanies the economic one, but the source does not specify an amount, a project, or a completion deadline.
### The relationship beyond the trade dossier The relationship also encompasses a human dimension, with Swiss communities in Thailand and Thai citizens in Switzerland, and a diplomatic dimension linked to 95 years of relations between the two countries. These elements show a bond broader than the free trade agreement alone; however, the communiqué does not link them to new rules or changes for citizens.
The visit is also part of the annual meeting of the Bretton Woods institutions, which in 2026 is being held «extra muros» in Bangkok rather than in Washington D.C., the seat of those institutions. The discussion of the World Trade Organization, the United Nations, and international Geneva places the economic dossier within a multilateral framework. For those operating in Switzerland, this means considering bilateral relations, economic cooperation, and diplomacy together, without turning the announcement into a domestic decision.
The Swiss business delegation will accompany Parmelin at both stops. It is a sign of economic interest in Thailand and Vietnam, not a list of company agreements already signed. Anyone in Switzerland who wants to follow the dossier can organize the information in a simple sequence. The aim is not to anticipate benefits, but to distinguish what has been discussed from what still needs to happen before entry into force.
### Five operational checks 1. Separate the two agreements. The one between EFTA and Thailand is the dossier discussed in Bangkok, with the steps still to be followed through entry into force. The one with Vietnam has the signing on October 18, 2026, as the scheduled event. The two paths should therefore be recorded separately.
2. Establish the timeline. October 15, 2026, identifies the meeting between Parmelin and Charnvirakul in Bangkok. October 17, 2026, concerns the welcome in Hanoi by Tô Lâm. October 18, 2026, is the date of the signing of the EFTA-Vietnam agreement. Using distinct dates avoids confusing talks, visit and signing.
3. Associate the dossier with the sector. Put the relevant item in a working sheet among production and automation, digital technologies, infrastructure and sustainable technologies. The grid derives from the press release and serves to track opportunities; on its own, it does not show that an activity is covered by the agreement.
4. Keep a separate section for climate. Note that Swiss interest concerns investments in Thailand in projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, under Article 6 of the Climate Agreement. Do not confuse a stated interest with an investment already made.
5. Add the international framework. WTO and reform, the United Nations, International Geneva, regional stability and the fight against criminal networks on the Internet are part of the broader discussion. They should be kept alongside, but distinct from, the economic sheet on the agreement.
### What to keep under observation The next step to be verified is the one indicated by the two interlocutors: how to bring the EFTA-Thailand agreement into force and how to make use of its opportunities. Monitoring must remain anchored in the information available on the dossier.
For the Swiss delegation from business circles, present in Thailand and Vietnam, participation signals the importance attributed to economic relations, but does not replace the identification of specific agreements. A sheet with date, sector, country and status of the agreement avoids conflating the Thai negotiation phase with the signing planned in Vietnam.
For a resident in Switzerland, this is a concrete way to follow the news without adding data not contained in the source: distinguish the events, classify the areas indicated and await the formal steps on entry into force.

## TL;DR - Customs changes effective from November 1, 2026 - Reliefs linked to the intended use of goods - Tares observations adjusted and R-17 published
## Key facts - Entry into force → November 1, 2026 - Publication → October 15, 2026 - Place → Bern - Scope → customs concessions for goods - Tariff → Tares - Regulation → revised version of R-17
As of November 1, 2026, important changes to customs concessions for goods in relation to their intended use will take effect. This forms the core of the external communication published on October 15, 2026 and dated Bern, October 15, 2026.
The announcement also provides for two further measures on that same date: the updating of the notes to the Tares customs tariff and the publication of the revised version of regulation R-17.
### The content of the announcement
The source therefore presents an update structured around three elements: customs concessions linked to the intended use of goods, the notes associated with the Tares customs tariff, and regulation R-17 in its revised version. The schedule is explicit: the communication was published on October 15, 2026, while the entry into force and the two adjustments are set for November 1, 2026.
The reference to intended use is the only criterion specified for describing the concessions. The text does not list the goods concerned, provide tariff codes, or indicate amounts, rates or forms. Nor does it attribute statements to individuals or authorities. These elements are not part of the notice and cannot be inferred from the entry-into-force date alone.
The wording concerning the regulation is equally precise: it does not announce a generic amendment, but the publication of the revised version of regulation R-17. For Tares, by contrast, the communication refers to the updating of the notes to the customs tariff. These are two distinct references, but they are presented as concurrent with the changes to the concessions.
For anyone who needs to track the update, the announcement therefore provides a schedule and the names of the texts to bear in mind. It does not yet offer a complete overview of the goods or the applicable conditions. The difference between October 15, the day of publication, and November 1, the day indicated for entry into force, is the clearest operational detail contained in the source. The same applies to the affected group: the source speaks of goods in general terms and does not indicate specific sectors, companies or categories. The rest will have to be read in the Tares and R-17 references cited in the announcement, without adding details that the communication does not report. The practical comparison enabled by the communication is primarily temporal, not quantitative. On October 15, 2026, the change was announced; November 1, 2026, is the date indicated for the changes to enter into force and for the two related updates. The source does not, however, make it possible to calculate a saving, a new rate, or a different customs duty amount.
### Before and after the announced date
| Item | Communication of October 15 | Announced date of November 1 | |---|---|---| | Customs reliefs | Changes announced | Enter into force | | Tares observations | Adjustment announced | Are adjusted | | R-17 regulation | Revised version announced | Is published |
This distinction avoids attributing more to the source than it says. The announcement establishes when the transition will take place, but does not quantify the effect on the goods. It does not specify amounts, percentages, tariff codes, or product categories. Therefore, the communication alone does not make it possible to determine whether a particular good qualifies for the reliefs or what treatment would apply.
The intended use is the variable indicated to describe the reliefs. A practical interpretation must therefore start with a description of how the goods are used, without replacing that description with a product name or an invented category. However, the release does not explain how to classify the intended use and does not provide examples: on its own, it does not make it possible to decide a specific case.
The same applies to Tares and R-17. Knowing that the observations will be adjusted and that the regulation will be revised indicates where to look for details, but does not reveal the content of the changes in advance. It is therefore not correct to turn the announcement into a list of exemptions, reductions, or compliance requirements. For anyone who needs to organize a review, the practical step is to compare the updated guidance with the intended use of the goods as of the announced date, keeping the two references cited by the source separate. To turn the announcement into an orderly verification, one can follow a sequence limited to the steps explicitly indicated by the source.
### Steps to follow
1. Set November 1, 2026 as the reference date for entry into force. 2. Identify, for each commodity concerned, the intended use to which the verification relates. 3. Check the observations on the Tares customs tariff after the announced adjustment. 4. Verify the publication of the revised version of regulation R-17. 5. Keep the Tares and R-17 references separate when reviewing the new concessions.
The first step serves to avoid confusing the date of the communication with that of the application. The text was published on October 15, 2026, but places the entry into force and the related updates on November 1. The publication date therefore serves as a notice; the November date as the announced operational reference.
The source does not indicate an office, form, portal or different deadline for individual commodities. It is therefore not possible to add a specific documentary procedure without going beyond the available text. The effect on a single commodity also remains linked to its intended use, which the announcement cites but does not detail.
In practical terms, it is advisable to prepare the verification in two parts: first read the adjusted Tares observations, then consult the revised version of regulation R-17 when it is published. The two references must be kept distinct because the source speaks of an adjustment to the observations in the first case and of the publication of a revised version in the second.
The most faithful procedure therefore consists in not anticipating content that is not present. Until November 1, the announced schedule remains available; from that date, the check should be based on the Tares and R-17 references mentioned in the communication, together with the description of the commodity’s intended use.

item.description: Puregym acquires the Swiss chain Nonstop Gym Puregym operates 49 gyms in Switzerland Nonstop Gym has 48 More than 100 facilities by the end of 2026
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Puregym acquires Swiss chain Nonstop Gym - Puregym operates 49 gyms in Switzerland - Nonstop Gym has 48 - More than 100 facilities by the end of 2026
## Key facts - Transaction → sale of Nonstop Gym to Puregym - Seller → Invision, based in Zug - Buyer → Puregym, based in Leeds - Objective → more than 100 gyms by the end of 2026 - Coverage → German-speaking Switzerland, French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino - Origin → Nonstop Gym was founded in 2014 in Geneva
## A merger that expands the network In Zurich, British competitor Puregym acquired the Nonstop Gym chain from Invision, a holding company based in Zug. The transaction is reshaping Switzerland’s fitness sector and effectively doubling the English group’s presence in the country.
Puregym currently operates 49 gyms in Switzerland, while Nonstop Gym has 48. The stated objective is to exceed 100 facilities by the end of 2026, extending the network to German-speaking Switzerland, French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino.
### Two brands, a national outlook The complementarity highlighted in the announcement is primarily geographical. Puregym also intends to make use of Nonstop Gym’s operational experience and organization. The acquired brand was founded in 2014 in Geneva and is intended to disappear in the long term.
The announcement issued on the occasion of the acquisition states: > “Together, we are creating an exceptional nationwide club network that could become number one in Switzerland and reach even more members”
For the British group, the acquisition represents a further step in its international expansion and pursuit of a leading position in the Swiss fitness market. Puregym is based in Leeds, England, and operates in six countries: it has 467 gyms in Great Britain, 128 in Denmark and 61 in the United States. Through a franchise partner, it also operates 23 fitness centers across Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
The scope described is national: the planned network includes the three areas mentioned in the announcement and aims for a broader and more coordinated presence across Switzerland. ## What changes on the Swiss fitness map
The practical impact of the deal lies in the possible concentration of a network spread across several areas of the country. The announcement describes Puregym and Nonstop Gym as geographically complementary chains. For the Swiss public, this formula indicates a project spanning German-speaking Switzerland, French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino, rather than remaining tied to a single area.
### A two-stage transition
The before-and-after comparison should be read carefully. Before the integration, there are two distinct brands, both present in the country; afterwards, the stated objective is a network of more than one hundred facilities, and the Nonstop Gym brand is intended to disappear in the long term. These are two different levels: the first measures the physical extent of the centers, while the second concerns the identity by which the network will be recognized.
The source places the quantitative objective by the end of 2026, but does not set a precise date for the disappearance of the brand. For those observing the local offering, this distinction avoids treating as already completed a process still described as an objective and transition. The growth of the network and the name change are therefore not the same step.
The third level is corporate. Puregym is majority-controlled by the US fund Leonard Green & Partners, while KKR has been among the shareholders since December 2021 with a significant minority stake. The presence of these investors places the acquisition within an international ownership structure, while the announcement presents it as a further step in the group's expansion.
For the national public, the useful point remains limited but concrete: follow the territorial integration and the transformation of the brand without attributing effects already achieved to the announcement. The ambition of a broader Swiss network is explicit; its completion remains tied to the stated horizon. ## How to follow the operation through the end of 2026
The source makes it possible to establish a simple check, useful for anyone who wants to follow the expansion without confusing announcements with results. The method does not require estimates: it is enough to keep the initial data, objective, geography, brand and financial information separate.
### Five steps for a rigorous verification
1. Establish the starting point. Record the Swiss presence of the two operators separately, because the announcement starts from two distinct networks. Do not automatically add up the clubs as if the new organization had already been completed: the final figure is indicated as a future objective.
2. Check the deadline. Use the end of 2026 as a reference point to verify progress toward a network of more than one hundred gyms. The deadline concerns the announced objective and must not be treated as a result already achieved.
3. Divide the territory into three areas. The communication mentions German-speaking Switzerland, Romandy and Ticino. This framework makes it possible to view the expansion without focusing only on Puregym's headquarters in Leeds or Nonstop Gym's Geneva origins: the stated project concerns the Confederation.
4. Follow the brand change. Nonstop Gym was founded in 2014 in Geneva and, according to the plan described, is destined to disappear in the long term. The wording does not set a precise date. It is therefore advisable to distinguish the brand transition from the network's numerical milestone.
5. Keep the financial dimension separate. The financial details of the operation have not been disclosed. When updating the news, only any data made public should be used, without attributing an undisclosed amount to the sale.
This procedure avoids two confusions: mistaking the target network for a result already achieved and interpreting the disappearance of the brand as an event occurring on a precise date. The source instead speaks of an objective to be achieved by a deadline and of a disappearance in the long term. The point to follow is the announced transformation of the network on a Swiss-wide scale.

## TL;DR - On September 10, 2026, SECO announces Mathias Cormann's visit. - On September 15, 2026, the OECD presents the report in Bern. - The report examines healthcare, pensions, labor, competition and housing.
## Key facts - Announcement → September 10, 2026 - Visit and conference → September 15, 2026, at 14:45 - Attendance confirmation → September 14, 2026, at 12:00 - Location → Federal Palace Media Centre, Bern - Participants → Mathias Cormann, Guy Parmelin, Karin Keller-Sutter, Helene Budliger Artieda, Ronald Indergand
### Announcement and appointment On September 10, 2026, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) announced the visit to Switzerland, scheduled for Tuesday, September 15, 2026, by Mathias Cormann, who heads the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) as secretary-general. During the working visit, meetings are planned with President of the Confederation Guy Parmelin and Federal Councillor Karin Keller-Sutter.
The central part will be the presentation of the OECD's latest report on Swiss economic policy. Cormann will present the document at a press conference, while Helene Budliger Artieda, director of SECO, will comment on the findings and recommendations from Switzerland's perspective. Ronald Indergand, head of SECO's Economic Policy Directorate, is also among the listed participants.
### The report's areas of focus The communiqué places the report within the context of the multiple challenges Switzerland must address. According to the OECD, action is needed to preserve the country's competitiveness and innovative capacity over the long term. The interventions listed include reforms in healthcare and old-age provision, reducing the administrative burden borne by companies, making fuller use of the workforce's potential and strengthening competition.
The topics examined also include adaptation to climate change and the availability of housing in Switzerland. The issues therefore concern national economic policy, while the source does not preview the detailed content of the individual recommendations. No amounts, new rules or implementation timetable are specified: these elements are not included in the press invitation.
### Schedule and access The event is scheduled for September 15, 2026, at 14:45, in the large conference room of the Federal Palace Media Centre, Bundesgasse 8-12, 3003 Bern. Access is restricted to journalists. SECO asks participants to confirm their attendance by Monday, September 14, 2026, at 12:00, by writing to medien@seco.admin.ch.
For readers in Switzerland, the invitation therefore sets out the date, venue and participants, while the report will be presented and commented on there. The source does not announce a decision already in force: it announces the presentation of the report and SECO's Swiss commentary. The practical point of the press release is the distinction between the topics identified and the measures that are still to be determined. The OECD identifies areas for action regarding competitiveness and innovation, but does not assign a specific measure to each. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the text makes it possible to identify priorities, not to infer a concrete change.
### A framework for reading the recommendations | Area | Source's indication | Detail not indicated | | Healthcare | Reforms in the healthcare sector | Content of the reforms | | Old-age provision | Reforms in old-age provision | Content of the reforms | | Businesses | Reduction of administrative burdens | Measures and timing | | Workforce | Better use of potential | Implementation methods | | Competition, climate change and housing | Strengthening of competition; analysis of adaptation to climate change and housing supply | Detailed recommendations |
The press release presents these indications as proposed measures and recommendations, not as changes already described in detail. It does not indicate an implementation timetable or differentiated implementation for the Cantons. Therefore, no different effects among territories can be inferred from the text.
For businesses, the keyword is the reduction of administrative burdens. For workers, the reference is the potential of the workforce. Healthcare, old-age provision and housing supply, on the other hand, are areas that the report links to the analysis of Swiss economic policy. The source brings these dossiers together under the objective of safeguarding competitiveness and innovative capacity, without establishing an order of priority.
Adaptation to climate change also enters the analysis, but is not accompanied by a list of interventions. SECO's commentary may be read alongside the findings and recommendations presented by Cormann; the press release, however, does not anticipate Helene Budliger Artieda's assessments.
The most cautious reading separates three levels: the area analyzed, the proposed recommendation and any measure with precise timing and procedures. The source offers the first two elements, but not the third. Attributing a concrete change to the report before its presentation would go beyond the information available. To follow the appointment without confusing the invitation with the decision, it is advisable to use SECO’s information as a checklist. The procedure indicated by the source is intended for journalists; no other means of access are described for the general public.
### Attending the conference 1. Send confirmation of attendance to medien@seco.admin.ch by Monday, September 14, 2026 at 12:00. 2. Check the appointment for September 15, 2026 at 14:45. 3. Go to the Federal Palace Press Center, large conference hall, Bundesgasse 8-12, 3003 Bern. 4. Bear in mind that the access indicated in the invitation is reserved for journalists.
The source does not request any other documents and does not indicate a procedure other than confirmation by email. It is therefore correct to follow the instructions contained in the invitation, without adding requirements that the press release does not mention.
### Following the report as a reader Those without access to the room can use the text as a framework for checking subsequent developments. The first step is to identify, in the report presented, the recommendations relating to the healthcare sector, old-age provision, businesses’ administrative burdens, the workforce and competition. The second concerns the analysis of adaptation to climate change and housing supply.
A simple method is to distinguish findings from recommendations and then check whether timelines or implementation procedures are indicated. If these details do not appear, only the general indication of the area for action remains. The same caution applies to the Swiss commentary: the press release confirms that Helene Budliger Artieda will comment on findings and recommendations, but does not report her assessments in advance.
### What to note on September 15 For an orderly reading, it is enough to record the topic addressed, the recommendation made and any operational detail actually presented. The objectives concerning competitiveness, innovation or better use of the workforce should not be turned into new rules. Until the conference, the source allows preparation to check the content, not anticipation of measures for Switzerland or individual Cantons.

## TL;DR - SEM reopens Niederscherli (BE) in mid-November. - The facility has 120 beds. - New applications are rising slightly for seasonal reasons. - Forecast for the end of 2026: 22 000 asylum applications; 10 000 concern S status.
## Key facts - Decision → State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) - Location → Niederscherli, Municipality of Köniz (BE) - Reopening → mid-November - Capacity → 120 beds - Primary destination → Ukrainian refugees - Forecast for the end of 2026 → 22 000 asylum applications; 10 000 concern S status - Closed centers → six, in June 2026 - Condition → closure of Niederscherli when applications start falling again
### The reopening announced by SEM On October 15, 2026, from Bern-Wabern, the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) announced the temporary reopening of the civil protection facility in Niederscherli, in the Municipality of Köniz (BE). The opening is scheduled for mid-November and provides 120 beds. The facility is intended primarily for Ukrainian refugees.
The decision comes after a slight increase, linked to seasonal factors, in the number of new asylum applications. The SEM points out, however, that the level remains contained and markedly lower than last year. The decline had made it possible to close six federal asylum centers in June 2026.
The reopening is not presented as a permanent expansion of the network. If the need for places should grow, the SEM can arrange additional beds by increasing occupancy density in other federal asylum centers. For the Niederscherli facility and any densification measures, the administration will proceed in consultation with the authorities of the municipalities concerned.
The plan also contains a return condition. As soon as the number of new applications starts falling again, the SEM will close Niederscherli again. For the time being, reopening other reception facilities is not planned.
The timetable indicated by the SEM unfolds in three stages: the reopening in mid-November, the quantitative estimate for the end of 2026 and the condition concerning the centers already closed, which extends at least into the summer of 2027. According to the SEM, around 22 000 asylum applications and around 10 000 applications concerning S status are expected by the end of 2026. The six centers closed in June 2026 will remain inoperative at least until the summer of 2027, provided that the number of new applications evolves as expected. ## A capacity that adapts to demand To understand the decision in operational terms, the key point is the flexibility of reception capacity. SEM does not describe a general reopening of the centers closed in June: it identifies a specific facility, with a defined capacity, and leaves open the possibility of increasing the number of places in other centers if needed. The comparison between the announced steps is as follows:
| Scenario | Planned measure | Condition | |---|---|---| | New applications showing slight seasonal growth | Reopening of Niederscherli | Mid-November and 120 beds | | Need for additional capacity | Densification in other federal asylum centers | Agreement with the municipalities concerned | | New applications declining | New closure of Niederscherli | No other facility planned for now | | Developments in line with forecasts | Six centers closed in June remain inoperative | At least until summer 2027 |
The picture compares a temporary response with a longer-term perspective. The Niederscherli facility is intended to address the slight seasonal increase without turning the forecast into a program to reopen all the centers. The source specifies that no additional facilities are currently planned to reopen and that the six closed centers will remain inoperative at least until summer 2027, if the expected developments are confirmed.
The numbers should also be read separately. The 120 beds describe the capacity of the facility becoming operational again; the 22 000 asylum applications and 10 000 applications for S status, on the other hand, are SEM's estimate for the end of 2026. Treating them as equivalent would lead to confusion between available places and projected applications.
### The role of the municipalities concerned The reopening of Niederscherli and any densification in the other centers will be implemented in agreement with the authorities of the municipalities concerned. Coordination with the local area is therefore part of the measure described by SEM.
For the reader, the practical implication is to follow the sequence, not just the overall number. Seasonal growth may activate temporary places; a decline in new applications leads to the closure of the facility; the absence of a new announcement, by contrast, means that the plan for the six closed centers remains in force. Planning remains tied to the trend in applications and the conditions set out by SEM. ## How to follow developments Anyone wishing to follow the matter in concrete terms can turn the announcement into a series of checks, without confusing the different deadlines.
### Five steps to monitor 1. Start with the operational date. The reopening is planned for mid-November: the first element to verify is therefore the temporary activation of the Niederscherli facility, not the reopening of the six centers closed in June.
2. Identify the capacity involved. The reference is the civil protection facility in the Municipality of Köniz (BE), with 120 beds, intended primarily for Ukrainian refugees. This defines the scope of the measure described by SEM.
3. Check for possible densification. If additional places are needed, SEM can arrange extra beds in the other federal asylum centers by modifying the available spaces. This operation should be considered together with coordination with the authorities of the municipalities concerned.
4. Check the trend in applications. The criterion indicated for closure is a return to a decrease in the number of new asylum applications. When this condition occurs, SEM will close Niederscherli again according to the announced plan.
5. Keep the two time horizons separate. By the end of 2026, SEM expects approximately 22 000 asylum applications and approximately 10 000 applications relating to S status; for the six centers closed in June 2026, the indicated horizon extends at least to summer 2027, provided the number evolves as expected.
This framework makes it possible to interpret updates without turning a temporary measure into a definitive decision. The source does not announce any additional reception facilities for the time being. Mid-November concerns the start, while the closure of Niederscherli is linked to a return to a decline in new applications.
To follow the matter, it is therefore advisable to compare each update with three elements: available capacity, the use of densification and any decline that would trigger the closure of Niederscherli. These are the indicators explicitly linked by SEM to the management of bed capacity.

item.description: Physioswiss submits 4'000 signatures in Ticino Request: at least 30% more for point values The mobilization involves all 26 cantons Submission
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Physioswiss hands over 4'000 signatures in Ticino - Request: at least 30% more on point values - The mobilization involves all 26 cantons - Handover in Bellinzona on October 15
## Key facts - Increase requested → at least 30% of tariff point values - Petition entitled → «For guaranteed physiotherapy close to home in the Canton of Ticino» - Date and place of submission → October 15, Bellinzona - Recipient → Fabio Lonni, head of political rights at the State Chancellery - Signatures collected → 127'000 in Switzerland, of which 4'000 in Ticino
The request is addressed to the cantonal authorities: fairer tariffs for physiotherapy services, so as to ensure accessible care close to home in the future as well. At the center is the increase of at least 30% in tariff point values.
The reference to geographic proximity accompanies the economic one: physiotherapy should remain guaranteed and close to home, while appropriate conditions for practices should enable fair salaries for professionals. Physioswiss presents these objectives as linked to the viability of the cantonal network. The problem is therefore described both from the perspective of practices and that of patients.
### The mobilization and the issue raised
Physioswiss maintains that the current remuneration does not make it possible to adequately cover practices' operating costs and ensure fair salaries for professionals. For the association, inadequate economic conditions would make it more difficult to maintain a widespread care network in urban centers, peripheral regions and rural areas.
The Ticino collection is part of a national mobilization that involved all 26 Cantons. The balance indicated by the mobilization is 127'000 signatures overall in Switzerland, with 4'000 collected in Ticino.
By submitting the signatures, Physioswiss urges the Department of Health to intervene within the limits of its powers, so that tariffs guarantee adequate coverage of the costs of services.
> «The support received highlights the importance, for the population of the Canton, of being able to access easily accessible physiotherapy. We hope that the Department of Health will take this signal seriously and work to ensure fair and sustainable funding for physiotherapy».
The association will monitor the development of cantonal tariff procedures and continue to support the sector's demands in discussions with the authorities. Physioswiss also emphasizes the contribution of physiotherapy to healthcare: the services can help avoid surgical interventions, shorten rehabilitation and safeguard patients' autonomy. ## The decisive point: point values
The debate does not stop at the new tariff system. Physioswiss has presented a system resulting from negotiations, which differentiates physiotherapy services in a more nuanced way. According to the association, however, this innovation alone is not sufficient to improve professionals' remuneration.
### Structure and values are not the same thing
The distinction indicated by Physioswiss is practical:
| Element | Function described by the association | |---|---| | New tariff structure | Represents physiotherapy services in a more differentiated manner | | Tariff point values | Determine the actual increases and are established in cantonal procedures |
For those observing Ticino's health policy, the decisive step is therefore the cantonal procedure. The petition does not merely call for a change in how services are represented: it calls for point values sufficient to cover the costs of the services. The 30% is the minimum threshold requested by Physioswiss in the petition.
If economic conditions made it possible to cover the costs of practices and ensure fair salaries, the stated aim would be to support a widespread network, in urban centers as well as in peripheral and rural regions. If conditions instead remained inadequate, according to the association it could become more difficult to maintain that presence close to patients' homes.
The distinction also helps in interpreting any future updates. A reference to the new tariff structure does not, on its own, clarify whether remuneration has improved. To understand whether the request produces a result, it is necessary to look at the point values established as part of the cantonal procedures and their ability to cover the costs of the services. It is on this step that Physioswiss focuses its discussions with the Department of Health.
Physiotherapy is also considered a component of healthcare whose effects go beyond the individual service: it can help avoid surgical procedures, shorten rehabilitation and safeguard patients' autonomy. For the association, the issue of tariffs therefore involves both the sustainability of practices and the continuity of the care network. ## Following developments without confusing the steps
To read the next updates in a practical way, it is useful to separate the tariff structure, point values and the role of the Department of Health. These are the three elements that Physioswiss's request links to remuneration and the resilience of the care network.
### The checklist to follow
1. Identify the subject of the update. Check whether the text concerns the newly negotiated tariff structure or the point values. The former represents services in a more differentiated way; the latter determine the actual increases.
2. Look for the reference to the cantonal procedure. According to Physioswiss, point values are established within the framework of cantonal procedures. This is the step to watch in order to understand how the financial request is progressing.
3. Check the cost criterion. The parameter indicated by the association is the ability of tariffs to cover the costs of services. Its complaint also includes the operating costs of practices and the possibility of ensuring fair wages for professionals.
4. Observe the commitment of the Department of Health. The petition asks it to take action, within the scope of its powers, to set appropriate tariffs. Its role is therefore one of the institutional steps to follow after submission.
5. Assess the effect on the network. Developments should also be considered in terms of the possibility of preserving care close to home in urban centers, peripheral regions and rural areas.
Physioswiss will follow developments in the cantonal tariff procedures and will continue to support the sector's demands in discussions with the authorities. For the reader, the practical takeaway is to focus on point values and their evolution, without confusing a new structure with an actual increase in remuneration.
The reason why the issue also concerns patients is indicated by the association itself: physiotherapy can help avoid surgical procedures, shorten rehabilitation and preserve autonomy. Economic sustainability is therefore linked to the possibility of maintaining a widespread care network.

item.description: The AELS-Malaysia referendum was formally successful.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The EFTA-Malaysia referendum has formally succeeded. - 60 347 signatures were submitted on October 5, 2026. - The Federal Chancellery found 59 866 of them to be valid. - The federal decree dates back to June 19, 2026.
## Key facts - Subject → economic partnership agreement between the EFTA States and Malaysia - Committee → referendum committee - Filing → October 5, 2026 - Signatures submitted → 60 347 - Valid signatures → 59 866 - Federal decree → June 19, 2026 - Publication → October 15, 2026 - Place → Bern
On October 15, 2026, from Bern, the Federal Chancellery announced the successful outcome of the referendum launched against the federal decree approving the economic partnership agreement between the EFTA States and Malaysia. This is the central fact of the notice, published on the same date.
The matter concerns a specific federal act: the federal decree of June 19, 2026, approving the economic partnership agreement between the EFTA States and Malaysia. The referendum committee submitted the signatures against that decree on October 5, 2026; the Federal Chancellery then determined which signatures were valid.
### Verification of the signatures
The referendum committee submitted 60 347 signatures. Among those submitted, the Federal Chancellery recognized 59 866 as valid. The press release therefore clearly distinguishes between the total number of signatures submitted by the referendum committee and the portion recognized as valid by the federal authority. The second figure is the one accompanying the official conclusion reported in the notice: the referendum was formally successful.
The result is not presented in general terms. The notice links the formal success to the verification of the signatures and identifies the contested act as the federal decree of June 19, 2026. The agreement, too, is identified precisely: it concerns the economic partnership between the EFTA States and Malaysia.
To read the announcement correctly, it is useful to keep the three elements reported separate: the referendum committee, which submitted the signatures; the Federal Chancellery, which determined their validity; and the federal decree against which the referendum was launched. The press release connects these steps in the sequence of October 5, 2026 and October 15, 2026, with reference to the decree of June 19, 2026.
The published information concerns the formal success of the referendum; it does not contain an assessment of the agreement. The news item should therefore be cited with the figures and dates reported by the Federal Chancellery kept together.
The definite significance of the announcement is therefore the formal success of the referendum. These are the facts communicated from Bern on October 15, 2026. ## The practical significance of the result
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the news provides a precise political and institutional fact. The statement attests to the referendum's formal success against a federal decree; the text provided does not indicate any further individual or economic effects. Staying within this scope avoids attributing to the announcement consequences that the source does not describe.
The correct reading depends on distinguishing between the agreement and the referendum. The federal decree of June 19, 2026 approves the economic partnership agreement between the EFTA states and Malaysia. The referendum, on the other hand, has been launched against that decree. The note therefore links the agreement to the contested federal act, while presenting the referendum's success as the outcome of the verification of the signatures.
For a national summary, the data to retain have different roles. October 5, 2026 marks the moment when the referendum committee submitted 60 347 signatures. October 15, 2026 marks the publication of the statement from Bern. The number 59 866, on the other hand, indicates the signatures that the Federal Chancellery found to be valid. Separating this information makes the text more precise and prevents the news from being turned into a prediction not contained in the source.
The journalistic value of the result therefore lies in the certification, not in an interpretation of the Agreement. A precise headline must indicate that the referendum succeeded and which decree it is directed against; it is not enough to refer generically to an agreement with Malaysia. ## How to report the news correctly
Anyone who needs to verify or summarize the case can follow an essential sequence, without adding elements external to the communication.
1. Begin with the date and place of the announcement: October 15, 2026, Bern. 2. Identify the subject: the referendum against the federal decree of June 19, 2026. 3. Link the decree to the economic partnership agreement between the EFTA states and Malaysia. 4. Report the filing of October 5, 2026, and the total of 60 347 signatures submitted by the referendum committee. 5. Separate that total from the 59 866 signatures that the Federal Chancellery found valid, ending with the communicated formula: the referendum has formally succeeded.
This sequence is sufficient for a brief, an informative headline or an update on federal politics. The final check consists in not confusing the number of signatures submitted with the number of valid signatures and in not attributing to the communication statements or consequences that were not reported. When the data are transferred into an article, the filing date should not be confused with the publication date. Likewise, the total number of signatures does not replace the figure for valid signatures.
The news, constructed in this way, preserves the subject, object, dates, figures and outcome without broadening the scope of the source.

item.title: Climate change: billions in costs for Switzerland by 2060
item.description: Climate-related damages are calculated through 2060 The comparison includes three climate scenarios Winter tourism will lose more than 2 billion a year Hydroelectric power
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Climate-related damages are calculated up to 2060 - The comparison includes three climate scenarios - Winter tourism will lose over 2 billion a year - Hydropower could grow slightly
## Key facts - Horizon → until 2060 - Scenarios → three - Risks analyzed → five - Winter tourism → annual losses exceeding 2 billion francs - Share of stations at risk → below 1’500-1’800 meters above sea level - Hydropower → slight increase in production
Until 2060, climate change will cost Switzerland billions. This is the result of a study commissioned by the Confederation, which estimated the damage under three different scenarios: one based on stringent climate protection, a second with measures of intermediate intensity, and a third characterized by an almost unchecked rise in temperatures. Five climate risks were assessed for each scenario.
### The risks considered
The calculation starts from the effects considered most relevant for the country: above all, heat waves and drought. Other phenomena examined include the shift of the snow line to higher elevations, heavy precipitation, storms and hail.
However, the study does not cover the full range of climate-related risks. Moreover, the researchers did not take the interdependencies between the various hazards into account in the models. If the effects reinforce one another, total costs for Switzerland could therefore be significantly higher than those calculated.
### Tourism, agriculture and energy
Winter tourism will have to contend with annual losses exceeding two billion francs until 2060. According to the study, ski resorts located below 1’500-1’800 meters above sea level will eventually have to close because they will not have enough snow, even under the most favorable climate scenario. Skiers may be accommodated at higher-altitude resorts, but adaptation will entail high costs in Alpine regions, including stabilizing cable-car stations and installing additional snowmaking systems.
For agriculture, the outlook is more favorable, but only if there is enough water and investment is made in irrigation. Hydropower production, on the other hand, could benefit slightly: less snowfall and more rain are expected in winter, despite more frequent periods of drought, especially in summer. Power plants will have to manage intense precipitation. The research thus indicates where it is worth investing in adaptation and where, as in lower-altitude ski resorts, investment does not offer the same prospects. The practical value of the research lies not only in the sum of the damages, but in the different exposure of the sectors. The estimates show that climate change does not have the same effect throughout the Swiss economy: winter tourism faces high losses, agriculture can contain damages provided one specific condition is met, and hydropower may record a slight overall increase. For anyone assessing an investment, this difference matters more than a single national figure.
### A map for adaptation
| Sector | Indicated effect | Response or condition | |---|---|---| | Winter tourism | Annual losses of over 2 billion francs | High-altitude locations, stabilized cable-car stations and additional snowmaking | | Agriculture | Contained damages if there is sufficient water | Investments in irrigation | | Hydropower | Slight increase in production | Management of intense precipitation |
In winter tourism, adaptation has a very concrete limit. Higher-altitude locations can welcome skiers, but stabilizing cable-car stations and adding snowmaking systems entails high costs, especially in Alpine regions. Lower-altitude resorts are instead identified by the study as cases in which investment in adaptation does not offer the same outlook. Location therefore becomes a decisive element in the assessment.
For agriculture, the favorable outcome remains tied to water availability. Irrigation can make it possible to contain economic damages, but the research does not present this outcome as a general go-ahead. The stated condition is precise and must remain central to any interpretation of the data.
Hydropower also shows a balance between benefits and costs. The slight overall increase in production comes alongside more frequent summer droughts and the need to manage intense precipitation. The positive balance therefore does not eliminate the investments required.
Caution is needed for all scenarios. Since interdependencies between hazards were not modeled, the risks could reinforce one another and push overall costs beyond the estimates. The comparison therefore serves to identify where and how much to invest, not to set a definitive limit on losses. ## How to use the estimates
The study can become a working framework for those who, in Switzerland, need to assess climate risks without assigning the same response to every sector. The process starts from the hazards measured by the research and keeps the conditions indicated for each activity separate.
### Four steps
1. **Isolate the risk.** Start with the five hazards analyzed: heat waves and droughts, rising snowline, heavy precipitation, storms and hail. The first check is to understand which of these elements concerns the sector being examined.
2. Compare the scenarios. Read the same sector across the three scenarios outlined by the study: rigorous climate protection, moderate interventions or a rise in temperatures almost without restraint. The comparison avoids basing the assessment on a single outcome.
3. Match the measure to the condition. In winter tourism, elevation and snow determine the outlook for resorts; in agriculture, irrigation requires sufficient water; in hydropower, managing heavy precipitation remains necessary even with a slight increase in production.
4. Consider combined risks. The calculation does not include interdependencies among the hazards. Every assessment must therefore leave open the possibility that the effects may reinforce one another and that costs may be higher than estimated.
This sequence makes it possible to distinguish between an adaptation indicated by the research and an expense that does not offer the same outlook. It also helps avoid reading the agricultural result as an unconditional guarantee or hydropower growth as an absence of costs.
The explicit horizon remains 2060. Therefore, the comparison should be kept within this period and linked to the chosen scenario. The operational questions are simple: which risk is being assessed, which measure addresses it, which condition must be present and which cross-effects remain outside the calculation?
To complement the analysis of climate costs with a look at everyday expenses, consult costo della vita in Svizzera.

item.description: AFC: information exchanged with 113 countries in 2026 Approximately 4 million accounts sent and received Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine joined No exchange
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - AFC: information exchanged with 113 states in 2026 - Approximately 4 million accounts sent and received - Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine joined - No data exchange with Russia
## Key facts - Date → October 15, 2026 - Institution → AFC - States involved → 113 - Registered financial institutions → approximately 9000 - Accounts sent → approximately 4 million - Accounts received → approximately 4 million - Legal bases in force → January 1, 2017
On October 15, 2026, the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (AFC) announced the exchange of information relating to financial accounts with 113 States. The operation falls under the global standard for the automatic exchange of information.
The group includes the 110 States already subject to the reporting obligation, joined this year by Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine. With 86 States, the exchange took place in both directions: Switzerland received and transmitted data. The other 27 sent information to our country without receiving any, as 14 are not yet considered to meet the international requirements for data confidentiality and security, while 13 voluntarily chose not to receive information. This year, too, no data was exchanged with Russia.
### A network involving thousands of institutions
Approximately 9000 reporting financial institutions are registered with the AFC. The group includes banks, trusts, insurance companies and other types of institutions. These entities collected and transmitted data to the AFC. The AFC sent partner States information on approximately 4 million financial accounts and received similar information on approximately 4 million. The AFC points out, however, that it cannot provide information on the amount of financial assets.
The information exchanged includes the identification of the account holder, account data and financial information. The elements indicated include name, address, country of residence, tax identification number, reporting financial institution, account balance and capital income.
Since January 1, 2017, Switzerland has had the legal bases necessary to apply the standard. The data transmitted enables the cantonal tax authorities to verify whether taxpayers have correctly declared financial accounts held abroad.
The communiqué thus presents the scale of the exchange through States, institutions and accounts, while keeping separate the data on the volume of financial assets, which the AFC does not quantify. ## Practical significance for Swiss taxation
For anyone who files a tax return in Switzerland and holds accounts abroad, the operational point is not the overall number of accounts, but the comparison between foreign information and what was declared. The source indicates that cantonal tax authorities can verify the accuracy of the tax return for financial accounts held abroad. The verification therefore concerns the correspondence between the taxpayer and the information communicated through the AFC.
### What data is included in the comparison
| Information | Practical interpretation | |---|---| | Holder, name, address and State of residence | Identify the person concerned | | Tax identification number | Link the data to the taxpayer | | Financial institution and account details | Identify the reported financial relationship | | Balance and capital income | Compare the financial information |
The table reprises the categories listed in the statement; it does not mean that the source quantifies a tax or the amount of the assets. On this point, the AFC is explicit: the figure of approximately 4 million accounts sent and approximately 4 million received does not make it possible to establish the total value of financial assets.
The number of countries does not replace individual checking: for the tax return, coherent information about the holder, the financial relationship and the economic data listed is what matters.
Reciprocity must also be interpreted precisely. For 86 states, the exchange took place in both directions. For 27, by contrast, Switzerland received information without transmitting any: 14 did not yet offer sufficient international guarantees regarding confidentiality and data security, while 13 had voluntarily declined to receive them. For a taxpayer, this means that not every country can be treated in the same way based solely on the total number of 113 states. The source also notes that there was no data exchange with Russia this year either.
The statement does not indicate tax rates, deadlines, penalties or amounts payable. Nor does it describe a different procedure for individual cantons. Its stated practical effect is more limited: to make available to cantonal authorities information useful for verifying the declaration of foreign accounts. ## The practical check: three steps
The communication does not indicate a new deadline for the taxpayer, nor does it list any forms or documents to submit. The action that can be inferred from the source is therefore an orderly review of one’s tax return, limited to financial accounts held abroad and information that may be subject to exchange.
### 1. Define the information to check
The first step is to compare the categories indicated by the AFC: identification of the account holder, name, address, country of residence and tax identification number. These should be supplemented with the account details, the reporting financial institution, the balance and capital income. There is no need to turn the number of exchanged accounts into an estimate of the assets: the source specifies that the AFC cannot provide information on the extent of financial assets.
### 2. Compare with the tax return
For each financial account held abroad, the check to perform is the one indicated in the communication: verify whether the taxpayer declared it correctly. The review should be understood as a comparison between the information available to the taxpayer and the data that may arrive through the automatic exchange. The text does not specify a box, format or deadline; it is therefore incorrect to invent additional instructions.
### 3. Bring a discrepancy to the attention of the cantonal authorities
When the comparison reveals a difference, the institutional reference indicated by the source is the cantonal tax authorities. The communication identifies these authorities as the body that can verify the correctness of the tax return. The AFC remains the federal point for the exchange: in 2026 it received and sent account-related information.
The date to use as a reference for the Swiss legal bases is January 1, 2017; the communication was published on October 15, 2026. To learn more about checking your tax position, consult the guide to dichiarazione delle imposte

item.title: HPV vaccine in Ticino: new system from January 1, 2027
item.description: From January 1, 2027 access to the HPV vaccine will change Coverage will shift to mandatory health insurance For ages 11-26 direct access to a doctor
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - From 1 January 2027, access to the HPV vaccine changes - Coverage shifts to compulsory health insurance - For ages 11-26, direct access to a doctor - In Ticino, over 38'000 people vaccinated over 17 years
## Key facts - Date → January 1, 2027 - Age → 11-26 years - Program → cantonal HPV vaccination - Coverage → mandatory health insurance - Deductible → exempt for vaccination and consultation - Tally → more than 38'000 people vaccinated - 2025 data → 3'355 first doses, average age 14
### From 2027, the new pathway
From January 1, 2027, the cantonal vaccination program against human papillomavirus will end in Ticino, but vaccination will not. The change was presented in Bellinzona by Giorgio Merlani, Ticino's cantonal physician, with one key point: it is not the Canton’s decision to stop paying for the vaccine.
This is a change decided at federal level: a cantonal program is no longer required for coverage by mandatory insurance. After 17 years of activity, the program becomes part of the ordinary system of recommended vaccinations.
From 2027, people between the ages of 11 and 26 can access vaccination more easily: they no longer have to go through a physician from the Cantonal Program and can go directly to a pediatrician, family doctor or any other physician in private practice. The organizational pathway therefore changes, while vaccination remains available.
The Canton will no longer manage vaccination directly, but will continue to support information and promotion. This support is aimed in particular at health professionals, adolescents and their families.
As for costs, mandatory health insurance will cover vaccination. HPV vaccination and the associated consultation, like other recommended vaccinations, will be exempt from the deductible. The percentage share provided for by health insurance will not change, however.
The tally for the 17 years also gives a measure of the activity: since the program began, more than 38'000 people have been vaccinated in Ticino. This vaccination prevents numerous forms of cancer. In 2025, 3'355 people received a first dose, with an average age of 14. ## Doses, coverage and uptake
### Schedule by age
The number of recommended doses depends on the age at which vaccination begins. The guidance for the new pathway is as follows:
| Age at start | Recommended doses | Specified period | |---|---:|---| | 11-14 years | 2 | Over at least 6 months | | 15-26 years | 3 | Over 6 months |
For those who start vaccination between ages 11 and 14, the recommended course comprises two doses, to be administered over a period of at least six months. If vaccination is started between ages 15 and 26, three doses are called for instead, to be completed over six months. Available scientific evidence does not indicate a need for booster doses.
The age at which vaccination is started is the first factor to consider when planning the course. The conclusion of the cantonal programme does not change these recommendations: it changes the route through which vaccination is accessed, which from 2027 no longer necessarily goes through a programme doctor.
The level of uptake is evident from the available data: in 2024, 71% of 16-year-old girls and 58% of 16-year-old boys had received two doses. According to the source, in both groups uptake exceeded the Swiss average recorded during the 2023-2025 period.
For the country, the goal is vaccination coverage between 80% and 90%, which should help reduce the disease burden and infection rates. The figure for 16-year-olds and this target refer to different levels: the former quantifies, within a specific age group, the proportion of people with two doses; the latter defines the coverage level to be achieved.
From an organisational perspective, the choice between a paediatrician, a family doctor or another doctor in private practice broadens the points of access. From a financial perspective, exemption from the deductible applies to both HPV vaccination and the consultation, while the percentage contribution provided for by health insurance remains in place. ## Operational steps from January 1, 2027
### A four-step procedure
1. **Identify the age group.** The first factor to consider is the age at which vaccination begins: between 11 and 14 years of age, two doses are recommended; between 15 and 26 years of age, three.
2. Choose the doctor. From January 1, 2027, it will no longer be necessary to consult a doctor in the Cantonal Programme. Access will be possible directly through one's paediatrician, family doctor or any other physician in private practice.
3. Organize the doses. For the 11-14 age group, the two administrations must be spread over at least six months. For the 15-26 age group, the three doses must be administered over six months.
4. Consider coverage. The vaccination and related consultation will be covered by compulsory health insurance. They will be exempt from the deductible, but the percentage contribution provided for by health insurance will remain unchanged.
The procedure described by the new organization therefore starts with the age group and continues with the choice of professional. No additional administrative step is indicated: the announced change concerns precisely the possibility of accessing the chosen doctor directly, without going through the cantonal programme.
After completion of the recommended doses, current scientific knowledge does not indicate the need for boosters. This element also makes it possible to view the process in a linear way: the number of doses and interval depend on the age at which vaccination begins, while no additional booster doses are planned according to the indications provided.
The Canton will nevertheless retain a role in informing about and promoting vaccination, with a focus on healthcare professionals, adolescents and their families. Direct management will pass to the ordinary system, while the Canton's information activities will continue.
