item.description: In September the index rises by 0,3% from August The annual decline remains at 0,2% Imports: +0,9% in the month and +2,1% year-on-year September inflation
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In September, the index rises by 0,3% compared with August - The annual decline remains at 0,2% - Imports: +0,9% in the month and +2,1% year-on-year - September inflation at 1,0%, compared with 0,8% in August
## Key facts - Period → September, monthly comparison with August - Total index → +0.3% monthly; annual decline of 0.2% - Producer prices → +0.1% monthly; annual contraction of 2.1% - Import prices → +0.9% monthly; +2.1% per year - Inflation → 1.0% in September; 0.8% in August; 0.4% in July - Forecast 2026 → between 0.6% and 0.9% - Forecast 2027 → between 0.6% and 1.1% - Diffusion → UST, with Keystone-ATS indication
In September, producer and import prices in Switzerland rose by 0.3% compared to August. The change was interpreted as a sign of greater pressure on business costs, fueled by the rise in prices of oil and other energy carriers following the wars.
The information was released this morning by the FSO, with the indication Keystone-ATS. On an annual basis, the index still recorded a decline of 0.2%, the 41st consecutive decline. The data thus compares a positive monthly movement with a still negative trend.
### The detail of the sub-indexes
The sub-index of producer prices, referring to indigenous products, marked a monthly increase of 0.1% and an annual contraction of 2.1%. Compared to August, oil products were the most expensive. The source distinguishes the variation of goods produced in Switzerland from that of imported goods.
The import price sub-index instead shows a progression on both horizons: +0.9% in the month and +2.1% on the year. In the monthly comparison, the increase mainly concerned petroleum products, crude oil and natural gas. The statement also mentions computers, vehicles and related spare parts among the goods that have become more expensive.
The FSO defines the producer and import price index as a cyclical indicator of supply and demand on the goods markets. The September photograph therefore combines the summary of the general index with the separate reading of the two sub-indexes.
The same update recalls that inflation stood at 1.0% in September, equal to 1% in non-decimal form, after 0.8% in August and 0.4% in July. The figure belongs to the different scope of consumer prices, but is reported together with the trend in company prices.
For the record of the data, the result is therefore not a single indistinct increase: the push of the month is more marked on imports, while the production component maintains a negative annual balance. It is the distinction used by the FSO to describe the situation. ## From statistics to consumer prices
For those who follow the cost of living, the index should be read as an upstream signal and not as the immediate measure of every expense. The FSO explains that production costs are normally passed on to final products; for this reason, the figure provides a useful reference for assessing the trend in consumer prices, that is, inflation. The transmission, however, is not linear: the index's fluctuations are significantly more pronounced, and it is more volatile because of its dependence on raw materials.
### The comparison that households and businesses need
A practical way to read it is to separate three questions: how much the total moved during the month, what direction domestic production took, and what pressure comes from imported goods. The source's figures can be set out as follows:
| Item | Monthly movement | Annual movement | |---|---:|---:| | Overall index | +0,3% | decline of 0,2% | | Producer prices | +0,1% | contraction of 2,1% | | Import prices | +0,9% | +2,1% |
The picture shows why the import figure deserves attention when oil and other energy carriers become more expensive: during the month, its change is positive both compared with production and with the total. This does not mean that every consumer price changes at the same time or to the same extent; the source warns that the business-goods index is more volatile.
The comparison with inflation reinforces the need not to confuse the indicators. In September, the consumer-price figure reached 1,0%, that is, 1%, after 0,8% in August and 0,4% in July. The source points to geopolitical developments to understand what follows, while the strong franc acts as a brake on imported price increases.
### Scenarios indicated by estimates
The cited forecasts do not offer a single figure. The economic actors listed by the source, including SECO, OECD, KOF, Economiesuisse, UBS and the International Monetary Fund, place the average increase between 0,6% and 0,9% in 2026 and between 0,6% and 1,1% in 2027. These are ranges, not results already observed.
Historical comparison helps measure the scale of the scenarios: average annual inflation was 1,1% in 2024 and 2,8% in 2022, the highest in 30 years. The last negative figure cited dates back to 2020, with a decline of 0,7%, shown as -0,7%. The sequence shows that the figure can move from a phase of rising prices to one of decline, while dependence on raw materials keeps volatility high. ## How to turn data into an operational reading
A prudent procedure can start with the UST update and always use the same sheet. The goal is to distinguish what the release measures from what it may indicate about the cost of living. There are four steps.
### Four steps
1. Set the comparison period. Note the month observed and the reference month: for the data considered, September should be read in relation to August. Separate the monthly movement from the year-on-year change, so the two time horizons remain distinct.
2. Separate the two subindices. Record producer prices and import prices in different columns. In the first case, look at domestic products; in the second, the imported categories indicated in the release, from energy to computers, through to motor vehicles and spare parts.
3. Add consumer prices alongside them. Place the inflation figure and the two previous months available in the source next to the business index: 1,0% in September, 0,8% in August and 0,4% in July. The comparison prevents the producer and import price index from being used as an automatic substitute for inflation.
4. Read the estimates as ranges. For 2026, the indicated range is between 0,6% and 0,9%; for 2027, between 0,6% and 1,1%. Note separately the possible effect of the strong franc and geopolitical developments, identified by the source among the factors to monitor.
To make monitoring repeatable, the sheet can contain five fixed rows: overall index, production, imports, inflation and the factors cited to explain the movement. With each new UST update, only the period is changed and the previous comparison is retained. The years 2026 and 2027 should be kept in the forecasts column, not in the column for results already verified.
This grid connects national data to everyday decisions about the cost of living without attributing a certain effect to a single change. For a tool dedicated to monitoring, see costo della vita in Svizzera.

## TL;DR - Amaudruz announces her candidacy in Geneva - She is the first confirmed candidate to succeed Parmelin - The election is set for December 9 - Deadline: October 23 at noon
## Key facts - Candidate → Céline Amaudruz - Party → UDC - Place of announcement → Geneva - Succession → Guy Parmelin - Application deadline → Friday 23 October, at midday - Election → 9 December - Age indicated → 47 years
On Thursday morning in Geneva, Céline Amaudruz, vice-president of the UDC and national councilor of Geneva, announced to the media her intention to run for the Federal Council. His is therefore the first confirmed candidacy to succeed Guy Parmelin, federal councilor of the UDC.
“I thought about the candidacy for a long time,” Amaudruz said. A possible election would make her the first female member of the UDC to enter the Federal Council, but this possible record still depends on the vote.
### A different decision from 2022
In the 2022 elections, following the resignation of Ueli Maurer, Amaudruz, now 47 years old, had not presented his candidacy. Now he has instead publicly declared that he wants to compete for Parmelin's succession; as a reason he reported that he had thought about the candidacy for a long time, without indicating other reasons.
Two weeks before Amaudruz's announcement, Parmelin had announced his resignation from the Federal Council, effective at the end of the year. The procedure therefore concerns the succession to the Vaud federal councilor and it will be up to the United Federal Assembly to choose his successor.
### The sequence of succession
The deadline for submitting applications is Friday 23 October, at midday. The election of his successor by the United Federal Assembly is scheduled for December 9. In the meantime, numerous names are circulating, but Amaudruz is the first confirmed candidacy reported in the source.
The news therefore delivers a precise sequence: announcement in Geneva, deadline for submitting candidacies and subsequent election. The text does not anticipate the outcome of the vote. At the moment, the verified fact is that Amaudruz intends to run for the position of federal councilor. The practical point for reading the news is to distinguish three levels: intention, confirmed candidacy, election. Amaudruz has announced that she intends to run; the source describes her as the first confirmed candidate; the decision rests with the United Federal Assembly on December 9. These three elements are not interchangeable. The first statement is not equivalent to the final result, while the presence of numerous names in circulation does not automatically turn each name into a confirmed candidacy.
### How to read the next steps
For those following national politics, the October 23 deadline at noon is the first operational reference. Until that deadline, the picture described by the source remains open to candidacies. The news does, however, already establish one position: Amaudruz is the first confirmed candidate, while the other names are mentioned only as names in circulation. Without a further list in the source, the same status cannot be attributed to the other names.
| Step | Information reported by the source | | Announcement | Céline Amaudruz, Thursday morning in Geneva | | Deadline | Friday, October 23, at noon | | Decision | United Federal Assembly, December 9 |
The table helps separate the calendar from the political assessment. October 23 is not the date of the election: it is the deadline for submitting candidacies. December 9 is not the date of Amaudruz's announcement: it is the date indicated for the election of the successor. The source does not describe intermediate steps other than those already indicated.
### The possible significance of the outcome
If she were elected, Amaudruz would be the first female representative of the UDC to join the Federal Council; however, the distinction remains only a possibility, since the vote has yet to take place.
Even the reference to the 2022 elections serves to assess the profile of the candidacy, not to predict the result. Amaudruz did not run then after Ueli Maurer's resignation; today, by contrast, she has announced her candidacy. The documented comparison ends there. The source does not attribute any preferences to the United Federal Assembly and does not indicate which name will be chosen. To follow the procedure correctly, the reader can use the dates and wording given in the source as a small checklist. The first criterion is linguistic: until the election, Amaudruz should be described as a candidate or as someone intending to run, not as an elected Federal Councillor. The source text in fact refers to the intention to run and links entry into the Federal Council to the possibility of being elected.
### Four useful checks
1. Verify the announcement: it took place on Thursday morning in Geneva, in front of the media. This identifies the moment when the candidacy was made public. 2. Note the deadline: Friday, October 23 at noon is the deadline set for submitting candidacies for the succession of the Vaud Federal Councillor. 3. Separate the names: the source mentions numerous names circulating, but calls Amaudruz the first confirmed candidate. Therefore, one must not present as already complete a list that the text does not enumerate. 4. Await the decision: the election of the successor by the United Federal Assembly is scheduled for December 9.
### How to formulate the scenarios
Before the December 9 vote, the only certain element is the announced candidacy; the outcome can be established only after the planned institutional step. If elected, Amaudruz would become the first female representative of the UDC to enter the Federal Council.
The timetable should be read together with Guy Parmelin's resignation, announced two weeks earlier and taking effect at the end of the year. This links the candidacy to a succession process that is already open, but does not anticipate the decision of the United Federal Assembly. For a correct update, three references are therefore sufficient: the October 23 deadline, the December 9 vote, and the actual outcome of the procedure. Until then, the most precise description remains that of the first confirmed candidate.

item.description: The average 3a rate fell to 0,21% in October Caisse d'Epargne d'Aubonne offers 1% 68 out of 93 institutions pay a maximum of 0,2% 500 francs per month for 30
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The average 3a rate fell to 0,21% in October - Caisse d'Epargne d'Aubonne offers 1% - 68 out of 93 institutions pay at most 0,2% - 500 francs per month for 30 years: 209'666 francs at 1%
## Key facts - Unweighted average rate in October → 0,21% - Previous comparison → 0,27% and 0,61% - Highest offer → 1% - Cornèr Banca → 0,7% - Third group → 0,65% - Average of ten major institutions → 0,14% - Bank Cler, Migros Bank, Raiffeisen and Valiant → 0,2% - PostFinance and Banca cantonale vodese → 0,05%
Moneyland.ch's analysis, reported by Keystone-ATS, finds an unweighted average of 0,21% for October on pillar 3a accounts. The figure signals a further reduction in remuneration for those who keep their pension savings in an account.
The report compares October's figure with the previous levels of 0,27% and 0,61%. According to the source, the trend reflects the general interest-rate environment and the reductions in the SNB's policy rate, which are gradually being passed on to 3a accounts as well. Ralf Beyeler, Moneyland expert.
### A wide gap among providers
The ranking shows clear differences: at the top is Caisse d'Epargne d'Aubonne, in French-speaking Switzerland, with 1%. Cornèr Banca is second at 0,7%, while Crédit Agricole Next Bank, Hypo Vorarlberg Bank, Pilla and Tellco share third place at 0,65%.
However, the majority of institutions remain far from the highest rates. Moneyland.ch analyzed 93 providers: 68 offer no more than 0,2%, and two others pay no interest at all. The analysis therefore shows that the choice of provider results in different rates being applied to the same type of product, the pillar 3a account.
Ralf Beyeler also notes that considerable sums are usually held in pension accounts. For this reason, the expert says, checking whether switching is worthwhile can leave more money available in retirement.
The picture also remains weak among the ten largest and best-known banks. The average for the group comprising the six Swiss banks active at a supraregional level and the four largest cantonal institutions is 0,14%. Bank Cler, Migros Bank, Raiffeisen and Valiant offer a rate of 0,2%; for PostFinance and Banca cantonale vodese, the figure falls to 0,05%. ## The impact of the rate on the final balance
### Two alternatives with different effects
The gap emerges above all in the final balance: Moneyland.ch illustrates it by assuming 500 francs paid every month for 30 years, thereby highlighting the effect of compound interest, which savers often underestimate.
The source's comparison can be read as follows:
| Source scenario | Balance after 30 years | |---|---:| | Account with interest of 0,05% | approximately 181'353 francs | | Account with interest of 1% | 209'666 francs | | Securities solution, average net return of 5,5% | approximately 445'000 francs, theoretically |
The final gap between the two bank accounts exceeds 28'000 francs. The calculation shows that the rate affects more than just the return for a single period: with regular deposits, the difference is reflected in the capital available in retirement. This is why the source urges readers not to underestimate compound interest.
The comparison then presents a riskier alternative: Moneyland.ch attributes significantly higher long-term returns to securities-based solutions in Pillar 3a. Retirement apps allow users to invest in well-diversified portfolios on relatively favorable terms. In the theoretical example, an average net return of 5,5% would bring retirement assets to approximately 445'000 francs after 30 years.
This figure is not guaranteed: if the markets perform poorly, the amount could be much lower. Investing in securities means being exposed to strong fluctuations and the risk of losses; those who still have many years before withdrawing the capital can generally withstand these ups and downs. Not all savers, however, react in the same way: when stock markets fall, some end up selling in a panic. For these customers, the source considers an interest-bearing account more suitable, even though it offers a lower return. ## How to move from assessment to decision
The operational process that emerges from the analysis separates two decisions: choosing the provider of the 3a account and deciding whether to stay with an account or switch to an investment solution. The source points out that the transfer can take place without difficulty and does not require changing your main bank.
### Four practical steps
1. Record the interest rate credited on your 3a account and compare it with the offers reviewed by Moneyland.ch. The analysis covers 93 institutions and shows how far apart the terms applied can be.
2. Consider another provider without confusing the 3a account with your main banking relationship. The transfer concerns the pension product: you do not need to change the bank you use for other transactions.
3. Measure the long-term effect using the example from the source: 500 francs paid in every month for 30 years. The comparison between an interest rate of 0.05% and one of 1% makes the impact of compound interest on the final balance visible.
4. Choose between an interest-bearing account and an investment solution based on your ability to tolerate fluctuations. Those who still have many years ahead can generally cope better with rises and falls, while those who might sell during a negative phase may be better off with an account, even if it offers a lower return.
This sequence avoids confusing the rate offered by the provider with the theoretical return of an investment strategy. The first comparison concerns the account’s interest rate; the second concerns market risk and your personal reaction to losses. Even a well-diversified portfolio, such as those offered by the pension apps mentioned by the source, remains exposed to possible negative performance.
The review can therefore start with your own account, continue with a comparison of the offers and end with a choice consistent with your savings horizon and your tolerance for fluctuations. To explore the topic further, consult terzo pilastro 3a.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/conti-3a-rendono-ancora-meno%2c-forti-differenze-fra-le-banche/92219474)*

item.title: Migros: new contract with 41 hours and 10% discounts
item.description: New Migros L-GAV for the 2027-2031 period From 43 to 41 hours with unchanged salary for many employees 10% discount on purchases from January 1, 2027 More
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR
- New Migros L-GAV for the 2027-2031 period - From 43 to 41 hours with unchanged salary for many employees - 10% discount on purchases from January 1, 2027 - Other sectors: wage measures of up to 0,7%
## Key facts
- Who → Migros and social partners - What → renewal of the national collective labor agreement (L-GAV) - Period → 2027-2031 - Hours → from 43 to 41 hours per week with unchanged salary - Coverage → even those who work less than 20% - Absences → entire net salary for 90 days, then 80% of the gross salary - Purchases → 10% in shopping vouchers from 1 January 2027 - Salaries → 1.6% overall; Food Retail up to 0.3%, other sectors up to 0.7%
### The agreement announced in Bern
The group announced on Thursday in Bern that Migros and its social partners have renewed the national collective labor agreement (L-GAV) for the period 2027-2031. The agreement introduces improvements in employment conditions relating to working hours, application of the contract, benefits in the event of illness or accident, purchases and wages.
To level the playing field within the group, the new agreement abolishes the sectoral agreements hitherto applied to logistics, meat processing and leisure. For many collaborators, working hours will drop from 43 to 41 hours per week, without changes in salary.
The new contract is not limited to full-time relationships. It will apply to all employees, regardless of employment level, including those working less than 20%. The source also indicates uniform benefits for illness or injury: the entire net salary will be paid in the first 90 days; 80% of the gross salary will then be paid.
From 1 January 2027, employees will be awarded ten Cumulus points for every franc spent, both on the entire range of Migros supermarkets and in the group's self-service restaurants. Migros quantifies the benefit as a 10% discount, provided in the form of shopping vouchers.
For 2027 the group has announced an overall investment of 1.6% of the wage bill, including specific increases for individual companies. In the Food Retail sector the national salary range can reach 0.3%, while for the other sectors the limit will be 0.7%. Individual companies will communicate their salary measures separately. Migros also specifies that its employees will continue to benefit from comprehensive social benefits.
The renewal therefore combines a contract applicable to all employees with measures that depend on the sector or the individual company. The reduction of hours is indicated for many collaborators, while the salary changes will be communicated separately. ## What changes in practice
### An agreement with different effects
The practical significance of the renewal does not lie in a single measure that applies equally to everyone. The source brings together four aspects: the harmonization of conditions across sectors, the reduction of working hours for many employees, the extension to every employment level, and wage measures differentiated by company and sector. For an individual employee, the first step is therefore to understand which part of the agreement concerns their employment relationship.
| Situation | Practical reading | | --- | --- | | Logistics, meat processing, leisure | The previous sectoral agreements are abolished. | | Many employees | The working-time reference changes from 43 to 41 hours, with unchanged salary. | | Employment level below 20% | The agreement also applies to those who work less than 20%. | | Illness or accident | Full net salary for 90 days, then 80% of gross salary. | | Food Retail and other sectors | Up to 0,3% in Food Retail and up to 0,7% in other sectors. |
This distinction is the correct way to interpret the 1,6% investment. The percentage concerns the overall wage bill and includes the specific increases of individual companies. The figure is not presented as an identical increase for every employee: the source indicates a national range of up to 0,3% for Food Retail, a percentage of up to 0,7% for other sectors, and specifies that individual companies will communicate their respective measures separately.
The transition between net salary and gross salary also requires separate consideration. The agreement specifies the full net salary for the first 90 days and 80% of the gross salary thereafter. Anyone reviewing a communication or payslip must therefore keep the two specified bases separate, without turning them into a single calculation.
The Cumulus benefit follows a different logic from the wage measures specified for 2027. The source presents it as a discount on purchases, provided in the form of shopping vouchers. The scope covers the entire range of Migros supermarkets and the group's self-service restaurants; Migros links the measure to easing employees' daily expenses.
The comparison helps distinguish three effects: time worked, treatment during an absence, and the benefit on purchases. To examine the pay items in more depth, one can consult busta paga svizzera. ## How to prepare for the new L-GAV
### The five-step check
The most practical way to follow the transition to the new agreement is to separate the general information from what the individual company must communicate. You can start with the conditions of your own employment relationship and create a simple checklist, without automatically attributing all announced measures to every employee.
1. Identify the sector of the employment relationship: logistics, meat processing, leisure, Food Retail or another sector. These are the areas referred to in the renewal and are used to interpret the wage measure that will be communicated by the individual company.
2. Note the employment percentage and working hours. If you are among the employees affected by the reduction, record the change from 43 to 41 hours with unchanged salary. Also note if you work less than 20%: the agreement will also apply in this situation.
3. Prepare a separate check for illness or accident: first 90 days with full net salary; subsequent period with 80% of gross salary. Keep the two bases separate when reviewing the applicable conditions.
4. From January 1, 2027, check which purchases are covered by the initiative. For every franc spent across the entire range at Migros supermarkets or in the group's self-service restaurants, you receive ten Cumulus points. The benefit, granted in the form of shopping vouchers, is equivalent to a 10% discount.
5. When the individual company communicates the pay measures, compare the content with the renewal benchmarks: total investment of 1,6%, range of up to 0,3% in Food Retail and up to 0,7% in the other sectors. Do not replace the company-specific figure with the overall figure.
A personal overview can bring together the sector, employment percentage, weekly hours, salary, treatment in the event of illness or accident and shopping benefit. These are the pieces of information that make it possible to distinguish the reduction in working hours, the rules governing absences, the shopping vouchers and the pay measure communicated by the company.
As for pay, the check must remain anchored to the communication from the individual company: the group has stated that the measures will be communicated separately and that employees will continue to benefit from full social benefits. This makes it possible to keep the general framework separate from the information relating to your own employment relationship.
To estimate the effect on your salary, use the calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.description: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford win the 2026 Nobel Prize The two teach at Stanford and Columbia University The studies concern stabilization
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford win the 2026 Nobel Prize - Both teach at Stanford and Columbia University - Their studies concern macroeconomic stabilization - Ernst Fehr does not receive the prize
## Key facts - Prize → 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics - Winners → Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford - Academic affiliations → Stanford and Columbia University - Citation → Microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization - Presentation → December 10 - Institution → Royal Bank of Sweden, 1968
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics was awarded on Monday to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, both American professors: the former teaches at Stanford, the latter at Columbia University. The award recognizes their studies on the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization.
The committee of the Swedish Academy explained that the models developed by the two economists have improved the ability to implement effective stabilization policies. The stated aim is twofold: to counter economic crises and keep inflation under control.
### The committee’s rationale
The research focuses on how firms and households respond to government measures and monetary policy interventions. According to the committee’s explanation, expectations about the future can mean that even the mere announcement of a measure by governments or central banks influences economic behavior. For the committee, therefore, policy transmission also depends on the reaction of these actors, not only on the formal content of a decision.
The Swiss figure in the story is Ernst Fehr, a Swiss and Austrian citizen, a professor at the University of Zurich and considered a leading figure in behavioral economics. His studies have helped temper the image of “homo economicus,” conceived as an individual driven solely by self-interest. Considered among the candidates for many years, Fehr was once again left empty-handed.
In 2025, Joel Mokyr received half of the award, while Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt each received a quarter. The prize recognized their work on the role of innovation as a driver of economic growth, with a rationale distinct from the one chosen for 2026.
The economics prize closes the series; its presentation also takes place on December 10, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel’s death. However, it is not part of the original Nobel Prizes: it was established by the Royal Bank of Sweden in 1968, on the occasion of its three-hundredth anniversary. ### What the research focuses on
For a reader following the Swiss economy, the practical value of the news lies in how to read public announcements. The source does not describe a new measure, but shows why a state decision or a monetary policy choice can also be assessed through the expectations it generates before its effects are felt.
The mechanism indicated by the committee can be summarized as follows:
| Point to observe | Reading offered by the source | |---|---| | Announcement | Even a communication can influence economic behavior | | Expectations | Expectations concern what companies and households anticipate for the future | | Subjects | The reaction concerns businesses and families | | Objectives | Stabilize the economy, counter crises and control inflation |
The distinction is useful because it separates the content of a measure from the response that measure may elicit. The source does not indicate the direction of every reaction and does not claim that an announcement always produces the same result. Instead, it says that expectations are part of how economic policy works. Therefore, when assessing news about inflation, it is not enough to look for the intervention already adopted: the message directed toward the future must also be considered.
For the Swiss public, the same caution applies when encountering references to BNS/SNB, the Federal Council or the Cantons. The source speaks of central banks and governments in general terms, not of these institutions. It does not even mention SECO or UST/BFS and does not provide data on the cost of living. Using these names to attribute concrete effects to a national measure would add information extraneous to the text.
The case of Ernst Fehr, on the other hand, offers an explicit and verifiable Swiss connection. The source presents him as a professor at the University of Zurich and as a prominent behavioral economist, but specifies that he did not receive the prize. The news therefore makes it possible to talk about his presence in the academic context described, not about a Swiss economic decision linked to the Nobel. ### A four-step check
To report the news correctly without turning it into an announcement of economic policy, one can follow a simple sequence.
1. Separate the recognition from the measure. The text concerns the awarding of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics to two professors, not the adoption of a new policy by a government or a central bank.
2. Check the recipients. The names are Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford; the respective institutions listed are Stanford and Columbia University. These elements identify the prize and prevent it from being confused with an award given to Ernst Fehr.
3. Read the full citation. The reference is to the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization. The committee’s explanation refers to economic crises, inflation, state intervention, monetary policy, and expectations for the future. These are the concepts to retain in the report.
4. Distinguish the calendar from the institution. The prize is presented on December 10, like the other awards in the series, but the source specifies that the economics prize is not among the original Nobels. Its establishment dates back to 1968, at the initiative of the Royal Bank of Sweden.
The final check concerns what must not be added. The news does not contain amounts, tax rates, tax deadlines, guidance for companies or households, or decisions concerning a canton. It therefore does not justify presenting the prize result as an immediate change for people living or working in Switzerland.
The sequence of the other awards should also be used only to orient the reader. The previous week, the winners in medicine, physics, chemistry, literature, and peace had been announced. In 2025, by contrast, the economics prize had gone to Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion, and Peter Howitt for their studies on the role of innovation in growth. ## TL;DR - UBS is assessing three scenarios for its headquarters outside Switzerland - The Council of States supports 100% CET1 capital - The current requirement for foreign subsidiaries is 60% - Additional capital is estimated at approximately 20 billion dollars
## Key facts - Source→Wall Street Journal - Scenarios→three - Current requirement→60% - Requirement supported→100% CET1 capital - Additional needs→around 20 billion dollars - Artisan Partners estimate→around 16 billion dollars - AT1 bonds written off→around 16 billion francs
UBS is reportedly evaluating various scenarios to move its headquarters out of Switzerland. The news was reported on Wednesday by the Wall Street Journal, which cited sources familiar with the matter and linked the hypotheses to the tightening of rules on capital requirements.
There are three options indicated. The first involves the acquisition of a US financial institution and the subsequent transfer of its headquarters to the United States. The second is a merger with a European competitor. The third consists of the acquisition of UBS by an American bank.
### The comparison on capital reserves
After the collapse of Credit Suisse in 2023, the provisions at the center of the story were formulated. The Council of States supported the obligation for the Swiss parent company to fully guarantee, through quality primary capital, i.e. CET1, shareholdings in foreign branches. The minimum requirement indicated today is 60%.
The measure aims to allow the bank to deal with any losses without resorting to state intervention. For UBS, however, full coverage could translate into additional capital needs of around $20 billion and weaken its international competitiveness.
Artisan Partners also described the new provisions as punitive and requested a transfer out of Switzerland. According to estimates by the US investor, the additional capital needed would be around 16 billion dollars.
Speaking on CNBC, Sergio Ermotti reaffirmed that keeping the headquarters in Switzerland would be advantageous for the national economy and for shareholders. However, Colm Kelleher warned that UBS could reconsider its presence in the country if the rules were too strict. The declared objective remains the achievement of a Swiss compromise.
Finally, the source specifies that UBS has not commented on the rumors about concrete plans to leave Switzerland. The scenarios reported by the Wall Street Journal therefore remain hypotheses linked to the comparison of capital requirements, not a transfer announcement already communicated. ## The issue for the Swiss financial center
The debate is not only about the registered office. The difference between CET1 and AT1 changes how the bank's safety is described. CET1 is capital immediately available to absorb losses. AT1 bonds, by contrast, can be written down or converted into equity only when certain conditions are met.
### Three readings of the same risk
During the rescue of Credit Suisse in 2023, AT1 bonds worth approximately 16 billion francs were completely written off. The transaction gave rise to legal disputes concerning the conditions and timing of the write-down. The debate thus pits those who consider CET1 a more reliable form of protection against those who still regard AT1s as an important additional instrument.
For a reader in Switzerland, the point to keep separate is therefore this: the political proposal concerns coverage of the parent company's foreign holdings, while the debate over AT1s concerns the functioning of a different safety instrument.
Financial estimates require the same caution. The approximately 20 billion dollars are the additional capital requirement attributed to UBS as a result of stricter coverage. The approximately 16 billion, by contrast, are Artisan Partners' estimate. The source presents them as different estimates of the capital needed, not as a single figure.
### Why an exit appears unlikely
Experts Simon Amrein and Peter V. Kunz consider an actual departure from Switzerland unlikely. Amrein points to political and economic stability, the strength of the currency, and the availability of qualified staff. A relocation could also hurt its reputation and client base. Kunz emphasizes the appeal of the Swiss Banking brand for wealthy international clientele, especially Asian and South American, and views the possibility primarily as a lever for political pressure.
The national impact identified by the source is therefore linked to UBS's position in the Swiss economy and the bank's international competitiveness. For the reader, the practical point is to follow the balance between capital soundness, the attractiveness of the financial center, and the headquarters remaining there: these are the effects and reasons highlighted by the source. ## How to follow the dossier without confusing the hypotheses
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the most concrete way to read the news is to separate the steps already reported from the consequences that are still only possible. The following sequence uses only the elements available in the UBS case.
### 1. Distinguish the source from the announcement
The Wall Street Journal reported the existence of alternative scenarios, citing sources familiar with the matter. UBS, however, did not comment on speculation about concrete plans to leave Switzerland. Before considering a transfer decided, it is therefore necessary to verify whether the discussion concerns reported hypotheses or an official position of the bank.
### 2. Identify the rule under discussion
The second step consists of establishing the numerical comparison: the minimum requirement indicated for holdings in foreign subsidiaries is currently 60%, while the Council of States expressed support for 100% coverage with CET1 capital. This is the regulatory point to follow, without automatically turning the Council of States' position into a final decision on the transfer.
### 3. Attribute each estimate
The approximately 20 billion dollars should be linked to the additional requirement reported for UBS. The approximately 16 billion dollars, on the other hand, belong to Artisan Partners' estimates. Maintaining this distinction avoids presenting either figure as a final amount or as a combined total.
### 4. Read CET1 and AT1 separately
CET1 is immediately available to absorb losses. AT1 depends on conditions for write-down or conversion. The precedent of the Credit Suisse rescue, in which approximately 16 billion francs of AT1 were wiped out, explains why the discussion on banking security cannot be reduced to UBS's headquarters alone.
### 5. Compare the possible outcomes
Finally, the three reported paths are different: acquisition of a US institution followed by a transfer to the United States, a European merger, or an acquisition by an American bank. They do not follow the same corporate path.
The useful question remains: what capital is required, from which entity, and through which instrument? This is the way to avoid confusing a corporate decision with a capital measure. To explore the operational side of banking relationships in the country, consult conti bancari in Svizzera.

## TL;DR
- In the canton of Bern, the rules depend on the competent authority - Institutions and categories of students may have different rules - Requirements, deadlines and amounts must be checked on the official source
## Key facts
- Topic → university fees in the Canton of Bern - Differences → institutions and categories of students - Competence → canton, municipality or competent institution - Check → requirements, deadlines and amounts on the official source
### The starting point: competence
In the Canton of Bern, university fees must be read starting from the institution that manages the individual case. The framework indicated by the source distinguishes between canton, municipality and competent institution: one of these levels can be the reference for university fees and integration programs.
For those preparing a registration, this changes the search method. It is not enough to look for a figure referring generically to Bern: you need to identify the official source of the competent canton or university and check the requirements, deadlines and amounts on that page. The same attention is needed when comparing different categories of students or institutions.
One category of student may follow a different rule than another, while two institutions may refer to different offices. The item to note, therefore, is not just the amount: the applicable category, any exemption, the available contribution and the deadline within which to act are also part of the verification. The official source remains the first step of registration.
The topic is part of the broader autonomy of the Cantons. In Switzerland there are three tax levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; the municipalities apply a multiplier on the cantonal tax. This fiscal architecture is used to read taxes, but does not in itself identify the university fee.
Even acronyms require a clear separation. The AFC/ESTV concerns direct federal tax and VAT; the cantonal administrations deal with cantonal and municipal taxes. The UFAS/BSV is linked to social security, including AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, and does not set taxes; the FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. For university fees, the reference remains the cantonal, municipal or university body indicated by the official source.
For the budget of those living in Switzerland, the distinction is concrete: a university item may require cantonal or institutional control, while the other items have different channels. Looking for a single answer in a single office risks confusing skills and procedures. ## Compare rules, not just figures
### Four checks before estimating the cost
The differences between university fees in the Canton of Bern cannot be managed with a comparison based only on the final amount. The useful question is what combination of institution, category of student, and relevant authority produces that rule. This interpretation avoids transferring a deadline found elsewhere to another registration or considering a contribution provided by a single institution valid for everyone.
| Element | What to check | Why | |---|---|---| | Institution | official source of the competent body | the rule may change | | Category | applicable student category | different conditions may apply | | Exemption | requirements indicated by the source | the benefit must be verified | | Contribution | competent cantonal body or university | conditions and deadlines count |
If a person moves from one institution to another, the verification must be repeated on the new official source. If the student category changes, it is not enough to maintain the previous calculation: any exemptions, contributions, requirements and deadlines must be checked again. When a cantonal page refers to the competent university, the reference is part of the procedure and should not be replaced with information found on a different source.
The budget must also separate university fees from the cost of living and other administrative items. For residents, KVG/KVG is compulsory health insurance to be taken out within three months of arrival. Premiums are per capita, vary by canton and region and may include a reduction in premiums through a cantonal subsidy. The KVG/KVG is neither a tax nor a salary contribution, therefore it should not be added or compared with the university fee as if it were the same item.
The same caution applies to social security. AVS/AHV, AI and BVG/BVG fall under social security, while the FSIO/BSV does not set taxes. Direct federal tax and VAT fall under the AFC/ESTV; cantonal and municipal taxes to cantonal administrations. Distinguishing these chapters allows us to better understand the cost of living without attributing to the individual university skills that belong to other bodies.
The correct comparison, therefore, is not between isolated numbers. It is between official source, applicable category, deadline and treatment expected for that specific registration. ## From verification to registration application
### Operating procedure
To transform information on university fees in the Canton of Bern into concrete practice, it is best to follow a short sequence that always refers to the official source.
1. Define the subject of the audit. Start from the registration and note whether the search concerns the tax, a possible exemption or a contribution. Keeping these elements separate avoids confusing an access condition with a reduction or support.
2. Identify the competent body. Check whether the reference page is that of the canton, municipality or university institution. If the first agency refers to another office, follow that referral and do not mix instructions from different sources.
3. Classify the student's position. The source predicts differences between categories of students and institutions; therefore the applicable category must be verified before reading amounts, requirements or conditions. Without this step, the comparison may refer to the wrong situation.
4. Record operational data. Requirements, deadlines and amounts must be obtained from the official source. The conditions for any exemptions and contributions must be sought in the same check. The useful data is not an isolated figure, but the combination of amount, term and requirement.
5. Double check before signing up. Before proceeding, compare the official page with the category identified and verify that the body indicated is the competent one. If the practice involves multiple levels, it maintains reference to each one without replacing the cantonal rule with that of another institution.
This procedure keeps the university fee separate from taxes and other expenses. For taxation, the AFC/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT, while the cantonal administrations deal with cantonal and municipal taxes. For pension provision, AVS/AHV and BVG/BVG belong to a different chapter. For those who are residents, the KVG/KVG must also be verified within three months of arrival, with rules on premiums and reductions managed at cantonal level.
After completing the checks, the comparison with the costo della vita in Svizzera helps place the university spending in the overall budget.

item.description: The gifts to Donald Trump were worth approximately 100'000 francs The delivery dates back to November 2025 US tariffs dropped from 39% to 15% A report on the authorities
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Gifts to Donald Trump were worth around 100'000 francs - The delivery dates back to November 2025 - US tariffs fell from 39% to 15% - A report on the federal authorities is expected by the end of the year
## Key facts - What → Rolex table clock and engraved gold bar - Indicated recipient → the American people - Who defended the initiative → Helene Budliger Artieda, director of Seco - Where → interview on the sidelines of an economic forum in New Delhi - Total value → approximately 100,000 francs - Legally binding agreement → talks still ongoing - Institutional review → Management Commission of the National Council - Expiration of the report → by the end of the year
### Seco's position
On October 14, 2026, Helene Budliger Artieda defended the gifts given to Donald Trump by a delegation of Swiss entrepreneurs. The director of Seco clarified that the initiative came from the private sector and that the watch and the ingot were not intended personally for the then 79-year-old president of the United States, but for the American people.
In an interview with Bloomberg TV, given on the sidelines of an economic forum in New Delhi, the outgoing secretary of state added that the gifts were registered at the White House. If all goes well, he explained, they will be destined for a presidential library. Budliger Artieda has resigned effective at the end of March 2027.
### The visit and the duties dossier
The delivery took place in November 2025, during a visit to the United States organized while the dispute over customs barriers was ongoing. The delegation went to Trump to negotiate and brought him a Rolex tabletop and an engraved gold bar, with a total value of around 100,000 francs.
The director described the participants as serious businessmen, convinced that they had acted within the framework of the legal provisions and after having carried out legal checks. Among them were Alfred Gantner, co-founder of Partners Group, Jean-Frédéric Dufour, number one at Rolex, and Johann Rupert, chairman of the board of directors of Richemont.
The matter remains open on a political-administrative level. The Management Commission of the National Council wants to examine the actions of the federal authorities in relation to American tariffs; the report is expected to be concluded by the end of the year. On the negotiation front, Seco says it is satisfied: since November 2025, when the reduction of US duties from 39% to 15% was announced, the United States has respected the agreement. Bern seeks security and calmer trade relations after the turbulent times following the tariff announcement on the so-called Liberation Day in April 2025. Talks for a legally binding agreement, however, continue. ## Practical reading for the Swiss economy
### The reference point for exporters
The figure that captures the change in the negotiations is the move in US tariffs from 39% to 15%, announced in November 2025. The source adds that the United States honored the agreement. For Swiss exporters, therefore, the concrete point is the level of the customs barrier specified in the negotiations, not the value of the gift delivered to the White House.
The two pieces of data belong to the same story but serve different functions: around 100'000 francs relate to the watch and gold bar; 39% and 15%, on the other hand, describe the reduction in US tariffs. Separating these elements prevents the delivery from being interpreted as an economic measure for residents. The source does not specify sectors, goods or companies and does not allow the effect to be extended to every Swiss activity. The group directly referred to is exporters, for whom Helene Budliger Artieda described conditions as difficult when stability is lacking in trade relations.
### Two timelines not to be confused
The dossier also has a second track. On the one hand, talks continue on a legally binding agreement between Switzerland and the United States; on the other, the National Council Control Committee is preparing a review of the federal authorities' actions in relation to US tariffs. The report is expected by the end of the year. The first track concerns the content of the trade barriers; the second concerns how the federal authorities handled the matter. The source does not yet present the outcome of either.
For those living in Switzerland, this distinction is the most solid practical takeaway: the text does not announce a new individual procedure. The effect described remains focused on trade relations and exporting companies. Bern is seeking certainty and calmer relations after the turbulent times that followed the tariff announcement of the so-called Liberation Day, in April 2025. As long as the legally binding agreement remains under discussion, the picture presented by the source is that of a reduction already announced and a negotiation that is still open. ## How to follow the dossier
### A five-step check
For a Swiss reader, the most concrete way to follow developments is to separate the information already available from the decisions still pending.
1. Identify which aspect of the news is involved. If the update concerns the watch, the gold bar or their registration at the White House, it refers to the private initiative delivered in November 2025. If it concerns the tariff percentage, it refers instead to the trade negotiations. 2. Check the tariff figure reported. The source uses the comparison between the initial 39% and the 15% announced after the agreement. This is the reference point not to be confused with the overall value of the gifts. 3. Verify the status of the agreement. The agreement on the reduction was honored by the United States, according to Budliger Artieda, but talks on a legally binding text are still ongoing. An update that refers to negotiations therefore does not amount, in the available text, to the conclusion of the agreement. 4. Follow parliamentary oversight. The Control Committee of the National Council is examining the actions of the federal authorities regarding US tariffs, and the report is expected by the end of the year. 5. Limit the conclusions to the parties mentioned. The source refers to Swiss exporters and trade relations with the United States; it does not mention forms, applications or personal deadlines for residents.
### What remains to be verified
This framework avoids two opposite errors: turning a private gift into a new economic measure or considering definitive a negotiation that the source still describes as open. For the Swiss exporters mentioned by the source, the issue to monitor is the customs barrier and any legally binding agreement; for the public, the institutional issue is the report on the actions of the federal authorities.
The available timeline remains clear: visit and gifts in November 2025, announcement of the tariff reduction in the same month, parliamentary report by the end of the year, and the director's resignation at the end of March 2027. These are the dates explicitly present for reconstructing developments, without adding procedures or effects that the source does not describe.

item.description: Attack on hundreds of French supermarkets Remote manipulation of refrigeration Damage amounting to millions of euros Coop and Migros: no similar attack recorded
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Attack on hundreds of French supermarkets - Refrigeration manipulated remotely - Damage amounting to millions of euros - Coop and Migros: no similar attack recorded
## Key facts - Target → refrigeration systems - Location → French supermarkets - Effect → higher temperatures and unusable food - Manufacturer → Danfoss, Danish company - Device status → obsolete generations without security updates - Switzerland → Coop and Migros have not recorded similar cases - Home → connected televisions, vacuum cleaners and speakers - Expert → Jean-Marc Seigneur, University of Geneva
A cyber attack that hit hundreds of French supermarkets has brought digital security into an infrastructure linked to food preservation. The pirates remotely manipulated the refrigeration systems, causing the temperature to rise.
Large quantities of food have thus become unusable. The damage caused by the attack amounted to millions of euros, according to the description of the episode.
The case reignites attention on the security of devices connected to the internet. The sequence described by the source is concrete: a system reached remotely was manipulated, the temperature rose and the food contents were no longer usable.
For the two Swiss chains the picture is different: Coop and Migros report not having encountered attacks of the same type. Migros adds that only a few of its stores use Danfoss refrigeration systems and that, for now, there are no signs of their involvement.
### The role of obsolete systems
The Danish manufacturer Danfoss, which makes many of the systems involved, explained that the affected devices are mainly of older generations and no longer benefit from security updates. The company thus drew attention to the conditions of the affected devices.
The threat also extends to private homes, where televisions, vacuum cleaners, speakers and other network-connected devices can provide an entry point for a cyber attack.
Connecting to the internet can leave any device exposed that does not have adequate protections and updates. The passage does not refer to a concrete domestic attack; instead, it signals possible exposure due to connection and insufficient protection.
This extension from commerce to homes is the national point of the story. Even for those living in Switzerland, the question is not just about refrigeration systems: it concerns the entire set of objects that can be connected to the network.
Jean-Marc Seigneur, an expert from the University of Geneva, recommends replacing default passwords, moving towards products from reliable companies and providing software and firmware updates. Finally, it invites us to evaluate whether it is really useful to make each device intelligent: each connected device introduces a further possible attack surface. ## Risk is not the same as an attack that has already occurred
The report makes it possible to distinguish three aspects. The first is the documented event: in French supermarkets, refrigeration systems were manipulated remotely, causing the temperature to rise and making food unusable. The second concerns the position of the Swiss companies mentioned: Coop and Migros have not reported similar attacks, while Migros currently has no indication that the few stores using Danfoss systems are involved. The third concerns homes: the source speaks of potential entry points, not a domestic attack that has already been documented.
### Three conditions to consider together
A device connected to the network is not automatically considered compromised. The source identifies a potential vulnerability when it is not adequately protected and updated. Danfoss's clarification adds a second element: a large share of the affected devices belongs to obsolete generations that no longer receive security updates. For the reader, the difference lies between the mere presence of a connection and the protection condition indicated in the source.
| Condition | Indication in the source | |---|---| | Device connected to the internet | May become a potential entry point | | Insufficient protection | The device may be vulnerable | | Now-obsolete generation | No longer receives security updates | | Making every device smart | Its actual usefulness should be assessed |
The relevant comparison for people living in Switzerland is not between an attack in France and a certainty in Switzerland. Coop and Migros have not reported similar cases, but the source does not present this fact as a guarantee for every connected device. At the same time, it does not describe a domestic attack that has already occurred: it mentions televisions, vacuum cleaners, speakers and other objects as potential entry points.
The practical consequence is a change in approach. The question is not only whether a device performs its function, but whether the connection provides a genuine benefit. Seigneur invites us to reflect on precisely this point: making every object smart introduces a new potential attack surface for every connected device. In this reading, the case of the French supermarkets becomes a reference point for assessing household choices without turning a possibility into an attack that has already been confirmed. ## The checklist for home appliances
The practical response indicated by the source consists of four guidelines for objects connected to the network. The sequence concerns both the appliances mentioned for homes and, more generally, any device connected to the internet: vulnerability depends on not being adequately protected and updated.
> “Replace default passwords, opt for products from reliable companies, and ensure that software and firmware are updated.”
### 1. Change the default password
The first check is to replace the default password. This measure should be considered for every object connected to the network, not just a refrigeration system. The source mentions televisions, vacuum cleaners, speakers and other household devices.
### 2. Choose a reliable company
When choosing a connected product, the expert recommends opting for reliable companies. This criterion is significant because Danfoss specified that a substantial share of the affected appliances comes from outdated generations that no longer receive security updates. The source does not provide a list of manufacturers or models: the guidance remains that of the expert, namely to favor reliable companies.
### 3. Keep software and firmware updated
The third step consists of keeping software and firmware updated. The recommendation concerns both, without separating software management from firmware management. For connected objects in the home, this is the indicated check for avoiding the vulnerability condition referred to by the source.
### 4. Assess whether the smart function is really needed
The fourth step concerns the initial choice. Seigneur suggests considering whether making every appliance smart is genuinely useful. If the function is not useful, the connection should not be considered automatic: every connected device adds a new potential attack surface. The checklist thus concludes with a decision before the technical one: protect and update what is connected, but first ask whether it needs to be connected.

## TL;DR - On October 14, 2026, the Federal Council approves Knifefish - Switzerland modernizes its electronic warfare capabilities - Knifefish facilitates procurement and exchanges with European partners - Neutrality remains guaranteed and withdrawal is possible
## Key facts - Decision → Switzerland's accession to the Knifefish MoU - Date → October 14, 2026 - Basic program → Sawfish, Swiss accession in November 2025 - Objective → acquisition of electronic attack systems - Participants → Netherlands, Germany and Denmark - Planned accession → Sweden through an amending agreement
Bern, October 14, 2026. The Federal Council gave its assent to Switzerland's accession to the memorandum of understanding on cooperation for electromagnetic combat capabilities intended for electronic attack, known as the Knifefish MoU.
The measure is part of the modernization of the Swiss Armed Forces' electronic warfare assets. The armed forces need systems capable of detecting, influencing or jamming electromagnetic signals. Switzerland is thus participating in a European program aimed at acquiring electronic attack systems.
### A program built with European partners
With Knifefish, the Netherlands is implementing a program to acquire these systems and facilitate exchanges with European partner states. Germany and Denmark are already participating in the initiative. Sweden intends to join through an amending agreement.
Switzerland's accession to the MoU stems from the Sawfish program, which Switzerland joined in November 2025. The latter concerns tactical electronic warfare systems, while Knifefish concerns electromagnetic combat capabilities for electronic attack.
The Federal Council links this new step to the armaments policy strategy of June 20, 2025. Among other objectives, the strategy provides for a targeted expansion of cooperation with neighboring states and other European partners. The decision of October 14, 2026, therefore brings together three elements already identified in the source: the modernization of the Swiss Armed Forces, European cooperation on procurement, and the connection with the Sawfish program. ## What changes operationally
The most concrete effect described in the press release concerns how military procurement is organized. Cooperation makes it possible to better coordinate materials and data, as well as to jointly use testing equipment and spare parts. For Switzerland, this model may translate into economies of scale and more advantageous purchase prices.
The advantage is not solely economic. Joint procurement strengthens interoperability between Switzerland and the European states participating in the cooperation. The source therefore indicates an operational benefit, linked to the possibility of making materials, data and equipment work together, and a logistical benefit, linked to the shared management of testing and spare parts.
### The three functions of electronic warfare
Electronic warfare uses the electromagnetic spectrum, which includes radio systems, radar and other electromagnetic signals. Its functions are distinct:
| Area | Function | |---|---| | Electronic attack | Reduces the ability of opposing forces to use the electromagnetic spectrum. | | Electronic protection | Protects its own systems from interference. | | Electronic support | Detects and analyzes signals. |
Knifefish concerns electronic attack; the Sawfish program, on the other hand, concerns tactical systems for electronic warfare. This distinction makes it possible to view the accession as an expansion of Swiss cooperation in a sector composed of multiple capabilities, rather than as a single type of equipment.
A precise political clause also remains in place. The MoU allows Switzerland to decide on a case-by-case basis which projects to participate in. Neutrality is guaranteed, and Switzerland may withdraw from the cooperation at any time if one of the states participating in the program becomes involved in an armed conflict. ## How to follow the next steps
The source makes it possible to reconstruct a precise institutional sequence, useful for avoiding confusion between the armament strategy, cooperation programs and individual projects.
### The sequence to follow
1. The first reference is the Federal Council’s strategy on armament policy, dated June 20, 2025. The document provides for targeted expansion of cooperation with neighboring states and other European partners.
2. The second step is Sawfish. Switzerland joined it in November 2025; the program concerns tactical electronic warfare systems.
3. The third reference dates back to October 14, 2026: on that date, the Federal Council approved Switzerland’s accession to the declaration of intent known as MoU Knifefish.
4. For each subsequent project, the case-by-case rule must be taken into account. Accession to the MoU does not automatically determine Swiss participation in every project: the source gives Switzerland the option to choose.
5. Finally, the condition related to neutrality must be verified. If one of the states participating in the program becomes involved in an armed conflict, Switzerland may withdraw from the cooperation at any time.
The certain date to follow is therefore that of the approval on October 14, 2026. The communiqué describes accession to the declaration of intent and the framework for cooperation, while the program’s objective is the acquisition of electronic attack systems. The procedure described is institutional: it concerns the selection of projects, coordination with partner states and the possibility of ending participation under the conditions indicated.
To understand future developments, the safest approach is to keep the three levels separate: the Federal Council’s strategy, the Sawfish program already linked to Switzerland and the new MoU Knifefish. This distinction avoids attributing to the decision content that the source does not indicate.

The expected deficit of the Canton of Graubünden for next year is close to 100 million francs. The pressure comes as contributions to third parties have increased by 24,8% over the last four years, an absolute increase of 296,3 million francs. Keystone-ATS asked what the reasons for this growth are.
### The items indicated by the Canton During today's press conference, the director of the Graubünden Department of Finance and Municipalities, Martin Bühler (PLR), clarified that the increases are not concentrated in a single area.
Comparing the 2023 actual accounts with the 2027 budget, the budget item recorded growth of 34,5%, amounting to 41,4 million francs. The main factor is individual reductions in health-insurance premiums. Since health-insurance premiums increase every year, the support needed to reduce them for insured persons in modest financial circumstances also grows and, consequently, so does the amount of the Canton's contributions.
In the sector comprising hospitals, healthcare facilities and nursing homes, contributions have grown by 10,9% since 2023. Factors driving expenditure include contributions for medical services governed by the Federal Health Insurance Act, as well as population ageing, a higher hospitalisation rate and the greater average severity of treated cases. From 2028, the transition to uniform financing of outpatient and inpatient services (EFAS) will entail additional costs of almost 20 million francs per year.
Over four years, spending on public transport has increased by 25,51 million francs, or 31,4%. The Canton attributes the increase to a decrease in federal funding and several investment projects, including those concerning Chur West railway station, Tiefencastel station and the Ilanz/Glion bus terminal. Moreover, in 2027, the implementation of Simon Gredig's (Greens) motion will affect costs and entail the transfer of burdens from the municipalities to the Canton, amounting to three million francs for 2027 and 2028.
For special education, the financial burden has grown by 45,5%, or 25 million francs. ## Reading budget pressure The increase in contributions to third parties should be read as the sum of different mechanisms. For anyone following a canton's accounts, the first practical distinction is between premium subsidies, healthcare services, regional transport and special education: the source brings them together in the same dynamic, but attributes different causes to each.
### Four mechanisms to separate | Item | Mechanism indicated | Time horizon | |---|---|---| | Individual premium reductions | Health-insurance premiums increasing and support for policyholders in modest economic circumstances | 2023 final accounts and 2027 budget | | Hospitals, healthcare facilities and nursing homes | Aging, higher hospitalization and greater severity of cases | From 2028 with EFAS | | Public transport | Reduction in federal funding and investment projects | 2027 and 2028 | | Special education | Integration projects, new jobs and employment percentages | Four-year period |
This separation avoids confusing premium growth with hospital expenditure. In the first case, the chain described is linear: rising health-insurance premiums, higher individual reductions and a greater cantonal contribution for insured persons in modest economic circumstances. The figure therefore concerns the relationship between premiums and support, not a single investment project.
For hospitals and nursing homes, the indicated factor is demographic and clinical: population aging is associated with a higher hospitalization rate and greater average severity of the cases treated. The outlook changes from 2028, when EFAS will entail almost 20 million francs per year in additional costs in the sector.
In public transport, the reading must take funding and investments together. The reduction in federal funding is indicated as the cause of the increase; several projects are cited in the same sector. The 2027 motion also makes the financial relationship between the Canton and the municipalities visible: the message quantifies the transfer of costs from the municipalities to the Canton at three million for 2027 and three million for 2028.
Special education follows a different trajectory: the Canton links the increase to the growth of integration projects, the creation of jobs and staff employment percentages. To read the budget without losing the causal link, it is therefore advisable to examine separately the item, the indicated cause and the year in which the increase has an impact. This breakdown shows how costs are distributed among insured persons, healthcare facilities, transport, municipalities and special education services. ## A practical procedure To follow the message about the budget without mixing data from different periods, the reader can use a simple sequence. The starting point is the time references cited by the source: 2023 actuals, 2027 budget and 2028 outlook.
### Four steps 1. Put the 2023 actuals in a first column and the 2027 budget in a second. This keeps the comparison anchored to the period used for the budget item that increased by 34,5%, amounting to 41,4 million francs. It should not be confused with the overall figure for contributions to third parties over the last four years.
2. Divide the items by cause. For individual premium reductions, note the annual increase in health-insurance premiums and the reference to policyholders in modest financial circumstances. For hospitals, healthcare facilities and nursing homes, note instead medical services, population ageing, hospitalisation and severity of cases.
3. Open a separate section for public transport. This should record the reduction in federal funding, the Chur West railway station, Tiefencastel station and Ilanz/Glion bus terminal projects, as well as the motion implemented in 2027. The transfer of costs indicated for the Canton is three million francs in 2027 and three million francs in 2028.
4. Keep the 2028 outlook distinct. The transition to EFAS will entail additional costs of almost 20 million francs per year in the healthcare sector. For special education, however, the review must instead follow integration projects, new jobs and staff employment percentages.
This framework helps prevent chapters that the Canton describes separately from being read as a single expense. For policyholders interested in the evolution of premiums, the operational step is to compare the health insurers with compare the health insurers.
